title: Nepal-Tibet floods: rescuers race to reach 900 people believed trapped in hydropower tunnels - The Guardian
description: Nepal-Tibet floods: rescuers race to reach 900 people believed trapped in hydropower tunnels  The Guardian
publisher.title: The Guardian
full_article:
Rescue teams are working to reach more than 900 people thought to be trapped in the tunnels and underground areas of half a dozen hydropower projects in Nepal following the devastating flash floods, ​the ⁠country’s disaster ​management authority said ​on ​Monday.

The death toll from the ⁠unprecedented deluge of ice, rock, mud ​and debris that crashed through valleys of Nepal on Wednesday last week has now risen to 903 people, with 16 more dead reported on the Tibet side of the border. More than 4,000 are missing in Nepal, with another 500 in Tibet.

Hundreds of bodies, many unidentified, have been buried in shallow graves on the plains ⁠of the Himalayan region after being swept down the mountains by the torrent.

Nepali officials said on Monday the focus was on reaching the 933 people missing from ‌hydropower projects in the flood-hit region.

Devastated by floods and overwhelmed by bodies, Nepalis weep for what remains of their homes Read more

Pictures and videos shared by rescue teams ⁠showed earth-moving equipment digging and shovelling mud to try to access the tunnels. “A large amount of debris has been deposited and that is posing us a big challenge to open the tunnels,” said Nepal army spokesperson Raja Ram Basnet.

Ashish Gurung, who normally works as a guide, was among the rescuers. “There is just mud everywhere,” he told the Guardian. “Inside the tunnel it was worse. It’s so difficult to move, the mud is so deep.”

On Sunday his team was trying to access Chilime Hydropower in Ruswana, in the worst-hit area.

Mountaineers improvised by grabbing planks of wood to check the depth of the mud, before using them as a makeshift bridge, along with a system of ropes to keep themselves safe, he said.

“Walking in it is very difficult; at one point it was up to our chests,” Gurung said. “We got close to the first station, about 130 metres in. Inside that far, you could [see further in]; it looked like it was just bodies.”

View image in fullscreen Ashish Gurung, left, with fellow rescue mountaineer Jenjen Lama at the Chilime Hydropower in Ruswana, Nepal. Photograph: supplied

The hydro company had given his team a map and it looked like there was a chance people in the tunnels could have survived by staying inside the internal infrastructure.

“They have a safe area inside,” he said. “Some of them could potentially be alive. I am hoping they are alive.”

Young girl rescued from rubble three days after Nepal flash flood – video

The Red Cross has ‌estimated that more than 90,000 people are likely to have been affected by the disaster, which China and some experts linked to the effects of the climate crisis.

Nepal’s prime minister, Balendra Shah, said the flood was an “unprecedented and devastating natural disaster” and it remained challenging to compile a complete assessment of the damage.

“Despite the adverse weather, difficult terrain and continuing risks, we are moving forward with determination to save the lives of our citizens,” he said in a Facebook post late on Sunday. Almost 21,000 security personnel were involved in the rescue operations, besides civilian workers and volunteers, he added.

Nepal’s disaster agency said on Monday that 903 deaths had been counted there, with 4,247 people, including 592 foreigners, missing. As of Sunday, Chinese authorities reported 16 deaths and 546 missing, and Chinese state media said 261 of the missing were foreigners, including over a hundred Nepalis.

China’s state-run CCTV reported that Beijing had mobilised more than 2,100 rescue workers and allocated at least ​220m yuan ($33m) to support relief efforts and had been airdropping equipment and supplies to frontline rescuers, while its soldiers used life-detection equipment to look for the missing.

View image in fullscreen Rescuers use diggers on Monday to clear way to a tunnel of the Trishuli 3A Hydropower project, following deadly flash floods and a mudslide, in Nuwakot district, Nepal. Photograph: Nepal Army/Reuters

Nepal has said it does not need foreign help in general search and rescue operations, but it has leaned on neighbours India and China for their expertise in tunnel rescues.

Rescue operations have been suspended several times since Friday because of bad weather and concerns that a lake formed across the Nepal-China border by the disaster could trigger fresh flooding after it began overflowing into Nepal’s rivers.

However, the weather was good on Monday and rescue ⁠work continued to pick up pace, said Narendra Pariyar, the district administrator of Rasuwa, one of the two hard-hit districts.

In the holy ​town of Devighat, on the banks of the Trishuli river that ​flooded, residents walked around the shells of what had once been ​homes, trying to salvage their belongings from the debris.

locator

The flood was “caused by glacier instability under the long-term effects of global warming”, Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported, saying ​it was a “new and prominent feature of cryosphere ‌disasters” on the Tibetan plateau.

Two ​Nepali officials told Reuters that China had ​not shared much information on glacier risks and water levels following a meeting to strengthen cooperation earlier this year, and they feared that a lack of data sharing could hamper future disaster preparedness.

China’s foreign ministry did not respond to a request for comment on the meeting.

रेड क्रॉस केरऽ अनुमान छै कि ई आपदा स॑ ९०,००० स॑ भी अधिक लोगऽ क॑ प्रभावित होय के संभावना छै, जेकरा चीन आरू कुछ विशेषज्ञ न॑ जलवायु संकट केरऽ प्रभाव स॑ जोड़लकै ।

नेपाल केरऽ प्रधानमंत्री बलेन्द्र शाह न॑ कहलकै कि ई बाढ़ एगो “अभूतपूर्व आरू विनाशकारी प्राकृतिक आपदा” छेकै आरू नुकसान केरऽ पूरा आकलन करना चुनौतीपूर्ण बनलऽ छै ।

नेपालक आपदा एजेंसी सोमदिन कहलनि जे, ओतय 903 गोटेक मृत्यु भेल अछि, जाहि मे 592 विदेशी सहित 4247 लोक लापता अछि। रविदिन धरि चीन के अधिकारी 16 के मौत आ 546 के लापता होय के खबरि देलक अछि, आ चीनी सरकारी मीडिया के कहनाय छनि जे लापता मे सं 261 गोटे विदेशी छथि, जाहि मे सौ सं बेसी नेपाली सेहो शामिल छथि.

चीन केरऽ सरकारी सीसीटीवी न॑ खबर देल॑ छै कि बीजिंग न॑ २,१०० स॑ भी अधिक बचावकर्मी क॑ जुटान॑ छै आरू राहत प्रयासऽ म॑ सहायता लेली कम स॑ कम २२० मिलियन युआन (३३ मिलियन डॉलर) के आवंटन करलकै आरू फ्रंटलाइन बचावकर्ता सिनी क॑ उपकरण आरू आपूर्ति हवाई ड्रॉप करी रहलऽ छै, जबकि ओकरऽ सैनिक न॑ लापता लोगऽ क॑ खोजै लेली जीवन-पता लगाबै वाला उपकरण के इस्तेमाल करलकै ।

नेपाल कहलनि अछि जे सामान्य खोज आ बचाव कार्य मे विदेशी मदद के जरूरत नहि अछि, मुदा सुरंग बचाव मे विशेषज्ञता के लेल पड़ोसी देश भारत आ चीन पर भरोसा केलक अछि।

खराब मौसम आरू आपदा स॑ नेपाल-चीन सीमा पार स॑ बनलऽ झील नेपाल केरऽ नदी म॑ उफन॑ लगला के बाद ताजा बाढ़ के शुरुआत होय सकै छै, एकरऽ चिंता के वजह स॑ शुक्रवार स॑ ही कई बार बचाव कार्य बंद होय गेलऽ छै ।

हालांकि सोमदिन मौसम नीक रहल आ बचाव ⁠काम गति बढ़ैत रहल, ई बात कड़ा प्रभावित दू जिला मे स एक रसुवा क जिला प्रशासक नरेंद्र परियार कहला।

पवित्र नगर देवीघाट में, बाढ़ि में डूबल त्रिशूली नदी के कात में, निवासी सब जे कहियो घर छल, ओकर गोला में घुमैत छल, मलबा सं अपन सामान बचाबय के कोशिश में.

चीनी सरकारी प्रसारक सीसीटीवी न॑ खबर देलकै कि ई बाढ़ “ग्लोशियर वार्मिंग केरऽ दीर्घकालिक प्रभाव के तहत ग्लेशियर अस्थिरता के वजह स॑ पैदा होय गेलऽ छै” आरू कहलकै कि ई तिब्बती पठार प॑ “क्रायोस्फीयर आपदा केरऽ एगो नया आरू प्रमुख विशेषता” छेकै ।

दू नेपाली अधिकारी रायटर क॑ बतैलकै कि चीन न॑ ई साल केरऽ शुरू म॑ सहयोग क॑ मजबूत करै लेली एगो बैठक के बाद ग्लेशियर के जोखिम आरू जल स्तर के बारे म॑ बहुत जानकारी नै साझा करलकै, आरू ओकरा आशंका छै कि डाटा साझा करै के कमी स॑ भविष्य म॑ आपदा के तैयारी म॑ बाधा आबी सकै छै ।

title: Second Israeli reported missing in Nepal six days after devastating floods - The Jerusalem Post
description: Second Israeli reported missing in Nepal six days after devastating floods  The Jerusalem Post
publisher.title: The Jerusalem Post
full_article:
A 41-year-old Israeli woman has been reported missing in the aftermath of the devastating floods that wrecked Nepal on Wednesday, killing nearly 800 people and leaving more than 3,000 people missing.

Israel's Consulate in Kathmandu and the Foreign Ministry's Situation Center are in contact with the missing woman's family and are working with local authorities in an attempt to locate her.

The woman, who Israel's Foreign Ministry identified as Katrina Sakowitz, is the second Israeli to be declared missing in Nepal. She holds both Israeli and Belarusian citizenship, and has lived in Milan for the last several years, according to KAN News. She was in Nepal as a tourist and did not identify herself as an Israeli citizen there, which KAN said is the Israel's Foreign Ministry did not identify her sooner.

On Thursday, tourism officials announced the first missing Israeli, noting that ZAKA had officially begun investigating their disappearance.

The Foreign Ministry released a statement on Thursday warning citizens to avoid traveling to the area due to the current natural disaster.

A drone view shows mud covering buildings and property following devastating floods at Trishuli in Nuwakot district, Nepal, August 27, 2026. (credit: REUTERS/Navesh Chitrakar)

Red Cross estimates over 90,000 affected

Nepal’s disaster management authority said that 933 people were missing from hydropower projects in the flood-hit region. The Red Cross estimates that more than 90,000 people are likely affected by the disaster, which China has linked to the effects of climate change.

Hundreds of bodies, many unidentified, have been buried in shallow graves as they began decomposing in the humid weather in the plains of the Himalayan country after being swept down the mountains by the torrent.

Beijing has said 261 foreign nationals from 23 countries were unaccounted for in Tibet, near a key border crossing with Nepal.

China’s state-run CCTV reported Beijing has mobilized more than 2,100 rescue workers and allocated at least 220 million yuan ($33 million) to support relief efforts and has been airdropping equipment and supplies to frontline rescuers, while its soldiers used life-detection equipment to look for the missing.

Rescue operations have been suspended several times since Friday because of bad weather and concerns that a lake formed across the Nepal-China border by the disaster could trigger fresh flooding after it began overflowing into Nepal's rivers.

सैकड़ों लाश, जेकरऽ बहुत पहचान नै छै, क॑ उथला कब्र म॑ दफना देलऽ गेलऽ छै, कैन्हेंकि हिमालयी देश केरऽ मैदानऽ म॑ नम मौसम म॑ धार स॑ पहाड़ऽ स॑ बहला के बाद सड़ना शुरू होय गेलऽ छै ।

नेपाल के साथ एक प्रमुख सीमा क्रासिंग के पास तिब्बत में 23 देश के 261 विदेशी नागरिक के बेहिसाब रहल बीजिंग कहलक अछि।

चीन केरऽ सरकारी सीसीटीवी न॑ खबर देल॑ छै कि बीजिंग न॑ 2,100 स॑ भी अधिक बचावकर्मी क॑ जुटान॑ छै आरू राहत प्रयासऽ म॑ सहायता लेली कम स॑ कम 22 करोड़ युआन (3.3 करोड़ डॉलर) के आवंटन करलकै आरू फ्रंटलाइन बचावकर्ता सिनी क॑ उपकरण आरू आपूर्ति हवाई ड्रॉप करी रहलऽ छै, जबकि ओकरऽ सैनिकऽ न॑ लापता लोगऽ क॑ खोजै लेली जीवन-पता लगाबै वाला उपकरण के इस्तेमाल करलकै ।

खराब मौसम आरू आपदा स॑ नेपाल-चीन सीमा पार स॑ बनलऽ झील नेपाल केरऽ नदी म॑ उफन॑ लगला के बाद ताजा बाढ़ के शुरुआत होय सकै छै, एकरऽ चिंता के कारण शुक्रवार स॑ ही बचाव अभियान कई बार स्थगित करलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

title: Arizona temple leader among missing in catastrophic Nepal flooding - AZ Family
description: Arizona temple leader among missing in catastrophic Nepal flooding  AZ Family
publisher.title: AZ Family
full_article:
TEMPE, AZ (AZFamily) — A revered spiritual leader from a Tempe temple is among thousands of people still missing after catastrophic flooding tore through Nepal and Tibet last week, killing at least 900 people

The floods were triggered by a glacial collapse high in the Himalayas so severe it registered as a magnitude 5.2 earthquake, sending a torrent of rock and water through valleys in Tibet and Nepal.

Sri Keshava Rao Tadipatri, a Sri Puttige Mutt Asthana Vidwamsaru affiliated with the Sri Venkata Krishna Kshetra Temple in Tempe, was traveling with a group of pilgrims on the sacred Kailash Manasarovar Yatra when the region was hit by Wednesday’s flash floods, temple leaders said.

The temple identified the following fellow pilgrims who were traveling with Tadipatri:

Anil Goel

Srinivas Sudhir Rangu

Mahendra Gupta

Laxminath Gopisetty

Kirti Acharya

Sudhindra Yapalparvi

Vivek Srivastav

Venkat Balasubramanyam

Venkat Bangalore

In a social media statement, the SVK Temple said families, friends and well-wishers are “anxiously” awaiting news of the group and asked the community to keep the pilgrims in their thoughts and prayers as they hope for their safe return.

“May Lord Sri Krishna, Sri Hari Vayu Gurugalu, and the blessings of Poojya Sri Puthige Swamijis, protect them and guide them safely back home,” the temple wrote.

The temple’s anxious wait mirrors a broader unease rippling through Arizona’s Nepalese community, home to roughly 2,000 Nepalese families.

“I’m finding more and more, a lot of people I know are missing,” said Gyan Nyaupane, a Chandler resident from Nepal. “I couldn’t even believe it. It was like watching movie. But unfortunately, it was real, right?”

“It’s super scary, to be honest. It’s very hard to describe,” said Gaurav Adhikari, a Tempe resident from Nepal.

The death toll from last week’s floods has risen past 900, Nepal’s disaster agency announced Sunday night. More than 5,000 people are still missing from Nepal and Tibet.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

नेपाल के चांडलर निवासी ज्ञान न्याउपाने कहलनि जे, हमरा बेसी स’ बेसी भेटि रहल अछि, हमरा जनैत बहुत रास लोक गायब छथि। “हमरा विश्वासो नहि भ’ रहल छल. ई त’ सिनेमा देखब जकाँ छल. मुदा दुर्भाग्यवश, ई असली छल ने?”

नेपालक टेम्पे निवासी गौरव अधिकारी कहलनि जे, ईमानदारी स’ कहब त’ सुपर डरावना अछि, एकर वर्णन करब बहुत कठिन अछि।

पिछला सप्ताह के बाढ़ि सं मृतक के संख्या 900 सं बेसि भ गेल अछि, नेपाल के आपदा एजेंसी रविदिन राति मे घोषणा केलक अछि. नेपाल आ तिब्बत सँ एखनहु ५ हजार सँ बेसी लोक लापता अछि ।

एहि रिपोर्ट मे एसोसिएटेड प्रेस क योगदान अछि।

हमरा लोकनिक कथा मे वर्तनी वा व्याकरणिक त्रुटि देखैत छी ? एकर रिपोर्ट करय लेल एतय क्लिक करू.

अहाँ लग कोनो ब्रेकिंग न्यूज स्टोरी के फोटो या वीडियो अछि? संक्षिप्त विवरणक संग एतय पठाबी।

By Gopal Sharma, Saurabh Sharma and Ethan Wang

KATHMANDU/BEIJING, Aug 31 (Reuters) - Nepal's rescue teams, helped by Chinese and Indian experts, stepped up efforts on Monday to reach hundreds of people believed to be stuck inside blocked hydropower project tunnels in the aftermath of last week's Himalayan flood.

The unprecedented deluge of ice, rock, mud and debris carved a trail of ‌destruction in the country's valley towns and villages, as well as across the border in China, on Wednesday, killing more than 900 people, with nearly 5,000 still missing.

A glacier collapse ‌is thought to have triggered the disaster.

Hundreds of bodies, many unidentified, have been buried in shallow graves as they began decomposing in the humid weather in the plains of the Himalayan country after being swept down the mountains by the torrent.

SEARCH TEAMS ​USE CONTROLLED BLASTS

Nepali officials said that the focus was on reaching the 933 workers believed to be trapped at 11 hydropower projects, including many who were working in about half a dozen tunnels, in the two hard-hit districts of Rasuwa and Nuwakot.

Pictures and videos shared by rescue teams showed earth-moving equipment digging and shovelling mud and rocks under lights in the dark of the night as workers watched. Soldiers used torchlight in a big pit they had created to look for space to get into one tunnel.

The Nepali army said search-and-rescue teams were using controlled blasts, excavators and searchlights to clear water and mud and reach trapped people. ‌Teams recovered three bodies after entering two tunnels, while other sections remained ⁠buried in mud and were still being searched, it said.

"A large amount of debris has been deposited and that is posing us a big challenge to open the tunnels," Nepali army spokesperson Raja Ram Basnet said. "Our main focus is on opening the tunnels."

NEPAL'S HYDROPOWER PROJECTS BOOM

On Monday, Nepali authorities said 903 people were ⁠confirmed dead, with 4,247 missing, including the 933 at hydropower projects. On the Chinese side, authorities said 16 people were killed in Gyirong County and 546 were missing.

The Nepali foreign ministry said that about 590 foreign nationals from 39 countries were still missing. More than 10,000 people had been rescued from the flood-hit region, including 323 foreign nationals, it added.

The Red Cross has estimated that more than 90,000 people were likely to have been affected ​by ​the disaster, which China has linked to the effects of climate change.

There has been a boom in hydropower projects ​in Nepal since the turn of the century as the mountainous country sought ‌to take advantage of its Himalayan water resources to address chronic domestic power shortages and exploit prospects for selling electricity to southern neighbour India.

Hydropower projects in Nepal's mountains need tunnels to carry water through the steep terrain, allowing developers to exploit the sharp elevation drop between Himalayan rivers and powerhouses to generate electricity.

Prime Minister Balendra Shah said the flood was an "unprecedented and devastating natural disaster" and it remained challenging to compile a complete assessment of the damage.

Beijing has said 261 foreign nationals from 23 countries were unaccounted for in Tibet, near a key border crossing with Nepal.

On Monday, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said that nearly 100 Chinese citizens have not been contactable on the Nepalese side.

A meeting of the Chinese cabinet urged all-out effort to search for the missing, the release of authoritative information, addressing risks ‌and hidden dangers and further improvement of emergency management capabilities, state television CCTV said.

RISK FROM LAKES AND LANDSLIDES

Although Nepal ​has said that it does not need foreign help in general rescue and search, it has leaned on giant neighbours ​India and China for their expertise in tunnel rescue.

Rescue operations have been suspended several times ​because of bad weather and concerns that a lake formed across the Nepal-China border by the disaster could trigger fresh flooding after it began overflowing into Nepal's ‌rivers.

On Monday, CCTV said that glaciers around an impact crater carved out near ​the site of last week's glacier collapse on the ​Nepalese side remained at risk of collapse. Drone footage showed multiple landslide deposits along both riverbanks, posing a risk of further collapses and the formation of new lakes, it said.

Last week's flood was "caused by glacier instability under the long-term effects of global warming", the state broadcaster reported.

Two Nepali officials told Reuters that China had not shared much information on glacier risks and ​water levels following a meeting to strengthen cooperation earlier this year, and ‌they feared that a lack of data-sharing could hamper future disaster preparedness.

The Chinese foreign ministry said that Beijing had continuously provided Nepal with meteorological and hydrological data and would ​continue to "strongly support" Nepal's disaster relief efforts and safeguard the two countries' common interests.

खराब मौसम आरू आपदा स॑ नेपाल-चीन सीमा पार स॑ बनलऽ झील नेपाल केरऽ नदी म॑ उफनै लगला के बाद ताजा बाढ़ के शुरुआत होय सकै छै, एकरऽ चिंता के कारण कई बार बचाव कार्य स्थगित करलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

title: Death toll from Nepal floods tops 900 - Washington Examiner
description: Death toll from Nepal floods tops 900  Washington Examiner
publisher.title: Washington Examiner
full_article:
The death toll from sudden and deadly floods in Nepal, China, and Tibet topped 900, with the total certain to rise considerably as rescuers try to reach those trapped by the disaster.

Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority put the latest number of confirmed dead at 903. Some of the bodies were recovered 150 miles from ground zero of the flood, which swept away thousands on Wednesday. The government put the number of missing at 4,250, and rescuers are currently focusing on reaching 933 missing people who are believed to be trapped in the tunnels of six hydropower projects.

In this photo released by Xinhua News Agency, rescuers use sniffer dogs to search for victims at a mudslide-hit area in Gyirong County, southwestern China’s Tibet Autonomous Region, Sunday, Aug. 30, 2026. (Jigme Dorje/Xinhua via AP)

“A large amount of debris has been deposited and that is posing us a big challenge to open the tunnels,” Nepal army spokesman Raja Ram Basnet said.

Advertisement

Rescuer Ashish Gurung told the Guardian that the rescue teams remain hopeful, as the hydropower company had provided maps of the underground infrastructure showing there were areas where they could be holding out. “They have a safe area inside,” he said. “Some of them could potentially be alive. I am hoping they are alive.” Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah said that nearly 21,000 security personnel were deployed for rescue operations, with many more civilian volunteers assisting. Advertisement “Despite the adverse weather, difficult terrain, and continuing risks, we are moving forward with determination to save the lives of our citizens,” he said late on Sunday. Nepal has relied on specialized tunnel rescue teams from China and India to help with the rescue. NEPAL WARNS OF POSSIBLE FRESH FLOODING AS COMMUNITIES GRAPPLE WITH DEVASTATION Advertisement Wednesday’s flood was caused when a massive 2,000-foot-wide piece of glacier broke off from high on a mountain, plunging 7,000 feet into a river and melting on impact. The glacier collapse and debris flow were so powerful that the U.S. Geological Survey originally labeled it as an earthquake, equivalent to a magnitude 5.2 earthquake. Hundreds of foreigners are among the thousands currently missing, including at least 85 American citizens.

नेपाल केरऽ राष्ट्रीय आपदा जोखिम कम करै आरू प्रबंधन प्राधिकरण न॑ ताजा मृतक के संख्या ९०३ बतैलकै ।बुधवार क॑ हजारों लोगऽ क॑ बहय वाला बाढ़ केरऽ ग्राउंड जीरो स॑ १५० मील दूर कुछ शव बरामद करलऽ गेलै । सरकार न॑ लापता लोगऽ के संख्या ४,२५० बतैलकै, आरू बचावकर्मी अभी ९३३ लापता लोगऽ तलक पहुँचै प॑ ध्यान केंद्रित करी रहलऽ छै, जेकरा प॑ मानलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै कि वू छह जलविद्युत परियोजना के सुरंगऽ म॑ फंसलऽ छै ।

अनुशंसित कहानी नेपाल के बाढ़ स॑ मृतक के संख्या ९०० स॑ ऊपर छै ट्रंप न॑ ‘खर्ग द्वीप क॑ उड़ाबै के वीडियो क॑ चकनाचूर करी देलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै’ मरीन ले पेन केरऽ आखिरी स्टैंड के वीडियो पोस्ट करलकै : नेशनल रैली केरऽ नेता न॑ पिछला तीन हार के बाद २०२७ केरऽ राष्ट्रपति चुनाव लेली बहुत आगू मतदान करी रहलऽ छै

सिन्हुआ न्यूज एजेंसी द्वारा जारी ई फोटो म॑ बचावकर्ता न॑ चीन केरऽ दक्षिण-पश्चिमी तिब्बत स्वायत्त क्षेत्र केरऽ ग्यिरॉंग काउंटी म॑ मडस्लाइड स॑ प्रभावित क्षेत्र म॑ पीड़ितऽ के खोज करै लेली सुंघै वाला कुत्ता के इस्तेमाल करी क॑ पीड़ितऽ के खोज करलकै, रविवार, ३० अगस्त २०२६ ।(जिग्मे डोर्जे/सिन्हुआ वाया एपी)

नेपाल सेनाके प्रवक्ता राजा राम बस्नेत कहलनि जे, भारी मात्रा मे मलबा जमा भ गेल अछि आ ताहि सँ हमरा सबके सुरंग खोलबाक पैघ चुनौती बनि रहल अछि।

बचावकर्मी आशीष गुरुंग न॑ गार्जियन क॑ बतैलकै कि बचाव टीम आशावादी बनलऽ छै, कैन्हेंकि जलविद्युत कंपनी न॑ भूमिगत बुनियादी ढाँचा के नक्शा उपलब्ध कराय देल॑ छै जेकरा स॑ पता चलै छै कि ऐसनऽ क्षेत्र छै, जहां वू टिकलऽ रह॑ सकै छै । ओ कहलनि जे, हुनका सब के अंदर सुरक्षित इलाका अछि। "ओहि मे सँ किछु संभावित रूप सँ जीवित भ' सकैत अछि, हम आशा क' रहल छी जे ओ जीवित छथि।" नेपालके प्रधानमन्त्री बलेन्द्र शाह बटैलै कि बचाव कार्यके लेल लगभग २१ हजार सुरक्षाकर्मी तैनात कएल गेल अछि, जाहिमे आरो बहुत रास नागरिक स्वयंसेवक सहयोग केने छल । विज्ञापन रविदिन देर राति ओ कहलनि जे, प्रतिकूल मौसम, कठिन इलाका, आ लगातार जोखिम के बावजूद हम सब अपन नागरिक के जान बचाबय के संकल्प के संग आगू बढ़ि रहल छी। नेपाल चीन आ भारत के विशेष सुरंग बचाव दल पर निर्भर रहल अछि जे बचाव मे मदद करत। नेपाल म॑ संभावित ताजा बाढ़ के चेतावनी छै, कैन्हेंकि समुदायऽ म॑ तबाही के सामना करना पड़ै छै विज्ञापन बुधवार केरऽ बाढ़ के कारण एगो पहाड़ प॑ २,००० फीट चौड़ाई के एगो विशाल ग्लेशियर के टुकड़ा ऊँचऽ स॑ टूटी क॑ ७,००० फीट नदी म॑ डूबी गेलै आरू टक्कर लगला प॑ पिघली गेलै । ग्लेशियर केरऽ पतन आरू मलबा केरऽ प्रवाह एतना शक्तिशाली छेलै कि यू.एस. एखन लापता हजारों मे सैकड़ों विदेशी शामिल छथि, जाहि मे कम स कम 85 अमेरिकी नागरिक सेहो शामिल छथि।

title: Hundreds feared stuck in hydropower tunnels as flood deaths surpass 950 in Nepal and China - AP News
description: Hundreds feared stuck in hydropower tunnels as flood deaths surpass 950 in Nepal and China  AP News
publisher.title: AP News
full_article:
KATHMANDU, Nepal (AP) — Rescuers raced Monday to free hundreds of workers believed to be trapped in tunnels at hydropower sites that were buried in mud by catastrophic flooding on the Nepal-China border , as the death toll climbed and increasingly desperate families searched for missing loved ones.

The combined deaths in Nepal and China surpassed 950, with more than 4,400 people missing. A private-sector association representing power companies said at least 900 workers were unaccounted for at 12 hydropower projects damaged by the flash floods in Nepal’s Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts.

About 500 of those workers were believed to be trapped in tunnels. At least one expert said that some workers could have access to oxygen, but others warned that the chances of finding survivors were diminishing. As the rescue efforts intensified, four bodies were recovered from three mud-filled tunnels, Nepal’s army said.

It was unclear whether rescuers have had any contact with the trapped workers since the initial calls for help.

Six days after the disaster, fears were growing that some might have suffocated, Dangi said.

Giant tunnels are built to control water flow

Rescue efforts were focused on people trapped in the gigantic tunnels built for controlling the flow of water.

“These tunnels are big enough to drive trucks through,” said Jakob Steiner, a geoscientist at the University of Graz in Austria based in Dhaka, Bangladesh. “And from what we understand, they have managed to get oxygen to some of those stuck inside and are trying to rescue them now. It’s a race for time, though, as people need food and water.”

In the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project, in the hard-hit Rasuwa district, at least 576 people were missing, Dangi said, adding that around 300 of them were believed to be trapped inside the project’s tunnel.

At the Trishuli-3 Hydropower Project, crews were working to descend about 15 meters (50 feet) into a tunnel in an effort to reach those believed trapped inside, according to Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet, Nepal’s army spokesman.

Workers shoveling mud from a flood-ravaged power station in Dhading, Nepal, told The Associated Press that the station is a key connection for providing power to over 20,000 people in the region.

Chinese media highlight government efforts to rebuild roads

On the Chinese side, rescue and recovery efforts included rebuilding the road leading to the Gyirong Port border crossing that regulated travel between China and Nepal.

Trucks carried giant rocks as workers tried to repave a portion of the road, state broadcaster CCTV showed Monday, next to rapidly rushing waters, which have been made more powerful by days of rain. The road is now under 2 to 3 meters (6.6 to 9.8 feet) of water. The repaving effort was just a little over a kilometer (0.62 miles) from the border, CCTV said.

Although some rescue teams have managed to reach the border, that represented only a portion of the force.

Chinese state media coverage has focused largely on the official response, highlighting the deployment of firefighters, the People’s Liberation Army and instructions from top leaders. Little is known about victims on the Chinese side.

राज्य प्रसारक सीसीटीवी न॑ सोमवार क॑ देखैलकै कि मजदूरऽ न॑ सड़क केरऽ एगो हिस्सा क॑ पक्का करै के कोशिश करतें हुअ॑ ट्रक विशालकाय चट्टान क॑ ल॑ जाय रहलऽ छेलै, जेकरा म॑ तेजी स॑ दौड़त॑ पानी के बगल म॑ छै, जेकरा दिन भर के बारिश स॑ आरू शक्तिशाली बना देलऽ गेलऽ छै । आब एहि सड़क पर 2 स 3 मीटर (6.6 स 9.8 फीट) पानि क नीचा अछि। सीसीटीवी के कहब अछि जे पक्की सड़क के प्रयास सीमा स मात्र एक किलोमीटर (0.62 मील) स किछु बेसी छल।

full_article:
Key points

Recent flash flooding is now Nepal’s deadliest natural disaster since the April 2015 earthquake

65,000 people require emergency water, sanitation and hygiene

More than 10,000 people have been rescued so far, including 252 foreign nationals

Triggered by a glacier collapse and landslide on Nepal’s border with China on Wednesday, the event is now Nepal’s deadliest natural disaster since the April 2015 earthquake that killed around 9,000 people.

As search and rescue efforts continue, UN agencies have begun to assess long-term needs, including more than 22,000 children needing protection, Mr. Dujarric said.

Struggling to reach hard-hit areas

Access remains the single biggest obstacle to the response, according to the UN emergency relief agency, OCHA.

Roads are passable only as far as Nuwakot, and some sections of highway linking Kathmandu to the hardest-hit areas remain completely blocked. Power has been restored in some areas.

Nepal’s Government has deployed more than 20,000 search and rescue personnel and declared a flood emergency in 15 municipalities, Mr. Dujarric said.

More than 10,000 people have been rescued so far, including 252 foreign nationals.

Tweet URL

Aid scales up

At the same time, World Health Organization (WHO) spokesperson Tarik Jašarević said overcrowding and disruption to water, sanitation and health services raise the risk of infectious disease outbreaks.

Recent OCHA assessments paint a similarly stark picture of humanitarian needs, including about 2,600 children under five expected to require treatment for severe wasting – or acute malnutrition – and around 10,500 pregnant and breastfeeding women needing nutrition assistance.

Some 19 schools have been damaged, nine completely destroyed and eight more being used to shelter displaced families while more than 10,000 school-age children require psychosocial support, OCHA reported.

Most urgently, preliminary reports indicate that 107 children may be separated from their parents or caregivers, leaving first responders to prioritise family tracing and reunification, according to Mr. Dujarric.

Disaster not yet over

Kamal Kishore, head of the UN Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR), highlighted the unprecedented nature of the glacier collapse and warned last week that “we are still coming to grips with the extent of the damage.”

The disaster has also affected the Tibet side of the border, where Chinese authorities report at least 16 dead and at least 546 still missing.

UN climate chief Simon Stiell said the disaster served as a reminder of how fragile mountain environments have become, noting that scientists and local communities have warned for years about the risks of climate change in the area.

“We also know a warming climate, driven by humanity burning colossal amounts of coal, oil and gas, is making tragedies like this one, and so many others around the world, much more likely, frequent and severe, with vulnerable communities often hardest hit,” he said.

What’s the UN doing?

Here’s a look at the ongoing response from UN agencies:

The World Food Programme (WFP) has dispatched nearly 80 metric tonnes of food, reaching about 9,200 people with assistance expected to last 15 days

The UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) has moved therapeutic food for about 500 severely malnourished children and mobilised 15 emergency medical teams

The UN’s humanitarian partners have set up a coordination hub in Nuwakot to strengthen planning and information sharing in the disaster response among organizations on the ground

Learn more about UN efforts in Nepal here.

प्रमुख बिन्दु

हाल के आकस्मिक बाढ़ि आब अप्रैल 2015 के भूकंप के बाद नेपाल के सबस घातक प्राकृतिक आपदा अछि

65 हजार लोक के आपातकालीन पानि, स्वच्छता आ स्वच्छता के जरूरत अछि

एखन धरि 252 विदेशी नागरिक सहित 10 हजार स बेसी लोक कए बचाउल गेल अछि

बुधदिन चीन के साथ नेपाल के सीमा पर ग्लेशियर के गिरला आ भूस्खलन के कारण शुरू भेल ई आयोजन आब अप्रैल 2015 के भूकंप के बाद नेपाल के सबस घातक प्राकृतिक आपदा अछि जाहि में करीब 9 हजार लोक के मौत भ गेल छल.

श्री दुजारिक नँ कहलकै कि जेना-जेना खोज आरू बचाव के प्रयास जारी छै, संयुक्त राष्ट्र एजेंसी नँ दीर्घकालिक जरूरतौ के आकलन करना शुरू करी देलकै, जेकरा मँ 22,000 सँ अधिक बच्चा सिनी क सुरक्षा के जरूरत छै ।

कड़ा प्रभावित इलाका तक पहुंचबा लेल संघर्षरत

संयुक्त राष्ट्र केरऽ आपातकालीन राहत एजेंसी ओसीएचए के अनुसार ई प्रतिक्रिया म॑ पहुँच एकमात्र सबसें बड़ऽ बाधा बनलऽ छै ।

सड़क केवल नुवाकोट तक गुजरय योग्य अछि, आ काठमांडू कए सबस बेसी प्रभावित इलाका स जोड़य वाला राजमार्ग क किछु हिस्सा पूर्ण रूप स अवरुद्ध अछि। किछु इलाका मे बिजली बहाल भ गेल अछि।

नेपाल सरकार २० हजार सँ बेसी खोज आ बचाव कर्मी तैनात केने अछि आ १५ नगरपालिका मे बाढ़िक आपातकाल घोषणा केने अछि श्री दुजारिक जानकारी देलनि ।

एखन धरि 252 विदेशी नागरिक सहित 10 हजार स बेसी लोक कए बचाउल गेल अछि।

ट्वीट यूआरएल

सहायता तराजू ऊपर

एकरऽ साथ ही विश्व स्वास्थ्य संगठन केरऽ प्रवक्ता तारिक जाशारेविच न॑ कहलकै कि भीड़भाड़ आरू पानी, स्वच्छता आरू स्वास्थ्य सेवा म॑ बाधा के कारण संक्रामक बीमारी के प्रकोप के खतरा बढ़ी जाय छै ।

हाल कें ओसीएचए आकलन मानवीय जरूरतक कें समान रूप सं शुद्ध तस्वीर पेश करएयत छै, जइ मे पांच साल सं कम उम्र कें लगभग 2,600 बच्चाक कें गंभीर बर्बादी – या तीव्र कुपोषण – कें इलाज कें आवश्यकता कें उम्मीद छै आ लगभग 10,500 गर्भवती आ स्तनपान करा रहल महिलाक कें पोषण सहायता कें जरूरत छै.

ओसीएचए के रिपोर्ट के अनुसार करीब 19 स्कूल क्षतिग्रस्त भ गेल अछि, नौ पूरा तरह सं नष्ट भ गेल अछि आओर 8 आओर स्कूल के इस्तेमाल विस्थापित परिवार के आश्रय देबय लेल कएल जा रहल अछि जखन कि स्कूली उम्र के 10 हजार सं बेसि बच्चा के मनोसामाजिक सहायता के जरूरत अछि.

सब सं जरूरी बात ई छै कि प्रारंभिक रिपोर्ट संकेत करै छै कि 107 बच्चाक कें माता-पिता या देखभाल करय वाला सं अलग कैल जा सकय छै, जेकरा सं फर्स्ट रिस्पांसर परिवार कें पता लगावय आ पुनर्गठन कें प्राथमिकता देनाय छोड़य छै, श्री दुजारिक कें अनुसार.

विपत्ति एखन धरि खत्म नहि भेल

संयुक्त राष्ट्र केरऽ आपदा जोखिम कम करै के कार्यालय (यूएनडीआरआर) केरऽ प्रमुख कमल किशोर न॑ ग्लेशियर केरऽ पतन केरऽ अभूतपूर्व प्रकृति प॑ प्रकाश डालतें हुअ॑ पिछला सप्ताह चेतावनी देलकै कि “हमरा सब क॑ अखनी भी नुकसान केरऽ हद के सामना करना पड़॑ लगलऽ छै ।”

ई आपदा स॑ सीमा केरऽ तिब्बत तरफ भी प्रभावित होय गेलऽ छै, जहां चीनी अधिकारियऽ न॑ कम स॑ कम १६ लोगऽ के मौत आरू कम स॑ कम ५४६ लोगऽ के अखनी तलक लापता होय के खबर छै ।

संयुक्त राष्ट्र केरऽ जलवायु प्रमुख साइमन स्टील न॑ कहलकै कि ई आपदा ई बात के याद दिलाबै के काम करलकै कि पहाड़ी वातावरण कतनी नाजुक होय गेलऽ छै, ई बात प॑ ध्यान देलकै कि वैज्ञानिक आरू स्थानीय समुदाय न॑ ई क्षेत्र म॑ जलवायु परिवर्तन के जोखिम के बारे म॑ सालौ स॑ चेतावनी देल॑ छै ।

हुनी कहलकै, “हमरा सब क॑ ई भी पता छै कि कोयला, तेल आरू गैस केरऽ भारी मात्रा म॑ जलाबै वाला मानवता स॑ संचालित गर्म होय रहलऽ जलवायु ऐसनऽ त्रासदी पैदा करी रहलऽ छै, आरू दुनिया भर म॑ एतना आरू, बहुत अधिक संभावना, बार-बार आरू गंभीर, जेकरा स॑ कमजोर समुदाय अक्सर सबसें जादा प्रभावित होय रहलऽ छै ।

संयुक्त राष्ट्र की क’ रहल अछि?

संयुक्त राष्ट्र के एजेंसी के तरफ सं जारी प्रतिक्रिया पर एक नजरि एतय देल गेल अछि:

विश्व खाद्य कार्यक्रम (डब्ल्यूएफपी) लगभग 80 मीट्रिक टन खाद्य पदार्थ भेजलक अछि, जे लगभग 9,200 लोक तक पहुंच गेल अछि आ सहायता 15 दिन तक चलबाक उम्मीद अछि

संयुक्त राष्ट्र बाल कोष (यूनिसेफ) लगभग 500 गंभीर रूप सं कुपोषित बच्चाक कें लेल चिकित्सीय भोजन स्थानांतरित करलक छै आ 15 आपातकालीन चिकित्सा टीमक कें जुटा देलक छै

संयुक्त राष्ट्र केरऽ मानवीय भागीदार न॑ जमीन प॑ मौजूद संगठनऽ के बीच आपदा प्रतिक्रिया म॑ योजना आरू सूचना साझा करै क॑ मजबूत करै लेली नुवाकोट म॑ एगो समन्वय केंद्र के स्थापना करलकै

नेपाल मे संयुक्त राष्ट्र संघक प्रयासक विषयमे बेसी जानकारी एतय प्राप्त करू ।

full_article:
Hundreds of pilgrims traveling to Mount Kailash were among those affected by devastating floods that struck the Nepal–Tibet border on Aug. 26, 2026. The floods destroyed the border crossing most commonly used to reach what is arguably the most revered holy mountain in the world, which sits in the Tibet autonomous region of China.

Mount Kailash is revered by Hindus, Buddhists and Jains. Rudolf Thalhammer/Moment via Getty Images

Hindus know the peak as the dwelling place of the god Shiva, Tibetan Buddhists as the abode of the deity Demchok, and Jains as the site where Rishabhanatha, their first spiritual teacher, achieved liberation. Today it also draws nonreligious travelers, who come for the harsh beauty of the landscape and the difficulty of the journey itself. Pilgrims and travelers do not climb Kailash. Instead, they walk a path roughly 33 miles around its base, which many believe to provide blessings and purification.

The legend of Kailash goes back thousands of years, to ancient Indian traditions describing a mountain at the center of the universe. But for most of that history, the Kailash of Indian literature was not associated with the peak that pilgrims travel to now.

In 2025, I published a book about Tibetan pilgrimage to Kailash. While researching it, I learned that it took centuries for a mythical mountain to become identified with this particular peak in western Tibet.

Kailash as legend

Indian religious texts describe a range of snowy mountains to the north called the Himalaya, or “abode of snows.” Beyond them, Indian cosmologies described a cosmic mountain called Meru, believed to stand at the center of the world.

The historian Alex McKay writes that the earliest mentions of a mountain named Kailash – Kailasa in Sanskrit – appear in the Hindu epics, composed roughly between the 4th century B.C.E. and the 4th century C.E.

In the “Ramayana,” an epic recounting of the god-king Rama’s search for his abducted wife, the monkey king Sugriva describes the far-off north, including Mount Kailash and Mount Meru. In the “Mahabharata,” an epic of dynastic war, the prince Arjuna visits a hermitage located on Mount Kailash.

However, these epics do not provide a specific location for Kailash. They portray it as a forbidding mountain realm of sages and gods, not as a pilgrimage destination for humans. The Mahabharata lists sacred places pilgrims should visit – sites across northern and western India – but Kailash is not among them. In fact, the epic states repeatedly that mere mortals cannot travel to the Himalayas.

It is in the “Puranas,” a body of Hindu religious texts composed between roughly the 3rd and 10th centuries, that Kailash is described as the abode of Shiva. The Puranas also begin to describe Kailash as the earthly form of the divine Meru. But it is still not a place of pilgrimage and still not fixed to a particular point on the map.

Kailash as physical place

An image showing Mount Kailash in the Ngari Prefecture of Tibet. Yongxin Wang/iStock / Getty Images Plus

Eventually, though scholars do not know exactly when, local traditions in North India began to identify particular peaks as Kailash. At least five different mountains, in the states of Jammu, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, have been claimed as the Kailash, and local pilgrimage to them continues today.

As Buddhism spread from India to Tibet beginning in the 7th century, Tibetans inherited Buddhist scriptures that spoke of Meru, Kailash and other sacred mountains. They also had their own long-standing practices of mountain veneration, making offerings to mountains that were believed to be the homes of local deities. Among them was the mountain now known as Kailash in western Tibet.

A mountain claimed

Tibetan traditions record that the geographical site of Kailash was claimed by practitioners of more than one religious tradition, and that the 11th-century saint Milarepa converted it to being a Buddhist site after defeating a non-Buddhist rival in a contest of magical power.

In the centuries that followed, Kailash became known as a particularly auspicious place to meditate and to visit on pilgrimage. Tibetans believed that while the mountain was the dwelling place of the deity Demchok, its true nature was only visible to the spiritually advanced. Any pilgrim who visited Kailash, known to Tibetans as Gang Rinpoche, would obtain blessings.

Even in Tibet, however, Kailash was only one pilgrimage site among many. Far more pilgrims visited the capital city of Lhasa.

The first clear reference to Indian Hindu pilgrims visiting the Tibetan Kailash comes in 1670, according to McKay, although earlier visits are possible. Its identity as the Kailash was not fully settled until the Indian subcontinent came under British colonial rule in the 19th century. Geographic surveyors mapping the border regions traced the sources of rivers such as the Indus to areas near Kailash. This matched ancient descriptions of Kailash as giving rise to rivers, and so the identification stuck.

By the 19th century, a small but steady flow of pilgrims traveled from India and Nepal, usually alongside the trade caravans crossing the Himalayan passes.

A pilgrimage closed and reopened

After China asserted control over Tibet in 1950, China and India negotiated official pilgrimage routes in a 1954 agreement. That arrangement did not last long. In 1959, a Tibetan uprising against Chinese rule was suppressed, and the Dalai Lama – the spiritual leader of Tibetan Buddhism – fled to India; religious life inside Tibet was severely restricted in the following years. In 1962, India and China fought a war over their disputed border, after which the border closed to Indian pilgrims for nearly two decades.

Routes reopened in 1981, and Tibetans were permitted to resume pilgrimage as well. But since then many Tibetans have found it difficult to obtain the necessary permits, and others have criticized excessive construction of hotels and roads at Kailash.

Most pilgrims today travel with private tour companies. Demand this year ran well above the Chinese government’s quota of 24,000 permits for Indian pilgrims. The Indian government also sponsors an official pilgrimage, with participants chosen by lottery, but places are limited to 1,000 people. Pilgrimage by Indian travelers had reopened only in 2025, after being suspended since 2020 because of COVID-19 and a deadly clash between Indian and Chinese troops in the Galwan Valley over the still-disputed India-China border.

Today, Kailash receives more pilgrims than at any point in its history. Most travelers from India now fly to Kathmandu and continue by bus through Gyirong, a road crossing between Nepal and Tibet that was expanded in 2014 and opened to international travelers in 2017. It became the most popular route after the 2015 earthquake damaged the main alternative. It was this crossing that the August 26 floods destroyed.

हिन्दू लोकनि एहि शिखर केँ शिव देवताक निवास स्थान, तिब्बती बौद्ध लोकनि डेमचोक देवताक निवासस्थान आ जैन लोकनि ओहि स्थलक रूप मे जनैत छथि जतय हुनकर पहिल आध्यात्मिक गुरु ऋषभनाथ मुक्ति प्राप्त केने छलाह | आइ ई गैर-धार्मिक यात्री सब के सेहो आकर्षित करैत अछि, जे परिदृश्य के कठोर सुंदरता आ स्वयं यात्रा के कठिनाई के लेल अबैत छथि | तीर्थयात्री आ यात्री कैलाश नहि चढ़ैत छथि । बल्कि एकरऽ आधार के चारो तरफ मोटा-मोटी ३३ मील के रास्ता पर चलै छै, जेकरा स॑ बहुत लोगऽ के मानना ​​छै कि ई आशीर्वाद आरू शुद्धि प्रदान करै छै ।

कैलाश के किंवदंती हजारों साल पहिने के अछि, प्राचीन भारतीय परंपरा स जे ब्रह्माण्ड के केंद्र में एकटा पहाड़ के वर्णन करैत अछि | मुदा ओहि इतिहासक अधिकांश भाग भारतीय साहित्यक कैलाश ओहि शिखर सँ नहि जुड़ल छल जतय एखन तीर्थयात्री लोकनि यात्रा करैत छथि |

2025 मे कैलाशक तिब्बती तीर्थयात्रा पर एकटा पोथी प्रकाशित भेल। एहि पर शोध करैत काल हमरा पता चलल जे पश्चिमी तिब्बतक एहि विशेष चोटी सं कोनो पौराणिक पहाड़क पहचान होबय में सदियो लागि गेल.

किंवदंती के रूप में कैलाश

भारतीय धार्मिक ग्रंथ में उत्तर में बर्फीला पहाड़ के एक श्रृंखला के वर्णन छै जेकरा हिमालय या “हिम के निवास” कहलऽ जाय छै । हुनका सब सँ आगू भारतीय ब्रह्माण्ड विज्ञान मेरू नामक ब्रह्माण्डीय पहाड़क वर्णन केलक जे विश्वक केंद्र मे ठाढ़ मानल जाइत अछि |

इतिहासकार एलेक्स मैके लिखै छै कि कैलाश नाम केरऽ एगो पहाड़ केरऽ सबसें पुरानऽ उल्लेख – संस्कृत में कैलासा – हिन्दू महाकाव्यऽ में मिलै छै, जेकरऽ रचना मोटा-मोटी ४वीं शताब्दी ई.पू. आ 4वीं शताब्दी ई.

देवराज राम केरऽ अपहरण करलऽ पत्नी केरऽ खोज केरऽ महाकाव्य “रामायण” म॑ वानर राजा सुग्रीव न॑ कैलाश पर्वत आरू मेरू पर्वत सहित दूर-दूर के उत्तर के वर्णन करल॑ छै । वंश युद्धक महाकाव्य “महाभारत” मे राजकुमार अर्जुन कैलाश पर्वत पर स्थित एकटा आश्रम मे जाइत छथि |

मुदा एहि महाकाव्य सभ मे कैलाशक लेल कोनो विशिष्ट स्थान नहि भेटैत अछि । एकरा मनुष्य केरऽ तीर्थस्थल के रूप में नै, बल्कि ऋषि-मुनि-देव केरऽ निषेधात्मक पर्वत क्षेत्र के रूप में चित्रित करै छै । महाभारत मे तीर्थयात्री कए जेबाक चाही से पवित्र स्थानक सूची देल गेल अछि – पूरा उत्तर आ पश्चिमी भारतक स्थल – मुदा कैलाश ओहि मे नहि अछि । असल मे महाकाव्य मे बेर-बेर कहल गेल अछि जे मात्र मर्त्य लोक हिमालयक यात्रा नहि क' सकैत अछि ।

मोटा-मोटी 3 आ 10 शताब्दीक बीच रचित हिन्दू धार्मिक ग्रंथक एकटा निकाय “पुराण” मे कैलाश केँ शिवक निवास स्थानक रूप मे वर्णित कयल गेल अछि | पुराण मे कैलाश के दिव्य मेरु के पार्थिव रूप के वर्णन सेहो शुरू भ गेल अछि | मुदा एखनो ई तीर्थस्थल नहिं अछि आ एखनो नक्शा पर कोनो विशेष बिन्दु पर स्थिर नहिं अछि.

भौतिक स्थान के रूप में कैलाश

तिब्बत के न्गारी प्रान्त के कैलाश पर्वत के दर्शाबै वाला एक छवि । योंगक्सिन वांग/आईस्टॉक / गेटी इमेजेज प्लस

अंततः भले ही विद्वान सब के ठीक-ठीक पता नै छै कि कखन छै, लेकिन उत्तर भारत के स्थानीय परंपरा में विशेष शिखर के कैलाश के रूप में पहचान करै लगलै। कम स कम पांच अलग-अलग पहाड़, जम्मू, हिमाचल प्रदेश आ उत्तराखंड राज्य मे कैलाश क दावा कैल गेल अछि, आ आइयो एहि ठामक स्थानीय तीर्थयात्रा जारी अछि।

जेना-जेना बौद्ध धर्म 7वीं शताब्दी स शुरू भ भारत स तिब्बत तक पसरल, तिब्बती कए बौद्ध शास्त्र विरासत मे भेटल जे मेरू, कैलाश आ अन्य पवित्र पर्वत क गप करैत छल । पहाड़ केरऽ पूजन केरऽ भी हुनकऽ अपनऽ पुरानऽ प्रथा छेलै, जेकरा में स्थानीय देवता केरऽ घर मानलऽ जाय वाला पहाड़ केरऽ प्रसाद भी छेलै । ओहि मे पश्चिमी तिब्बत मे आब कैलाश के नाम सँ जानल जाय वाला पहाड़ सेहो छल |

एकटा पहाड़ दावा केलक

तिब्बती परंपरा में दर्ज छै कि कैलाश के भौगोलिक स्थल पर एक स॑ अधिक धार्मिक परंपरा के साधकऽ के दावा छेलै, आरू 11वीं सदी के संत मिलारेपा न॑ जादुई शक्ति के मुकाबला म॑ गैर-बौद्ध प्रतिद्वंदी क॑ हराबै के बाद एकरा बौद्ध स्थल म॑ बदली देलकै ।

एकर बादक शताब्दी मे कैलाश ध्यान आ तीर्थ यात्राक लेल विशेष रूप सँ शुभ स्थानक रूप मे जानल गेल | तिब्बती लोकनिक मानब छलनि जे ई पहाड़ जखन कि डेमचोक देवताक निवास स्थान थिक, एकर असली स्वभाव मात्र आध्यात्मिक रूप सँ उन्नत लोक केँ देखबा मे अबैत छल | जे कियो तीर्थयात्री कैलाश जे तिब्बती लोकनि गंग रिंपोछे के नाम सँ जनैत छथि, हुनका आशीर्वाद भेटैत छलनि |

मुदा तिब्बत मे सेहो कैलाश कतेको तीर्थस्थल मे मात्र एकटा तीर्थस्थल छल । राजधानी शहर ल्हासा मे कहीं बेसी तीर्थयात्री आयल छलाह ।

तिब्बती कैलाश केरऽ दौरा करै वाला भारतीय हिन्दू तीर्थयात्री केरऽ पहिलऽ स्पष्ट संदर्भ मैके के अनुसार १६७० म॑ आबै छै, हालांकि एकरा स॑ पहल॑ के दौरा संभव छै । कैलाश के रूप में एकरऽ पहचान पूरा तरह सें नै बसलऽ छेलै जब॑ तलक कि १९वीं सदी में भारतीय उपमहाद्वीप ब्रिटिश औपनिवेशिक शासन के अधीन नै आबी गेलऽ छेलै । सीमावर्ती क्षेत्र के नक्शा बनाबै वाला भौगोलिक सर्वेयर न॑ कैलाश के पास के इलाका तक सिंधु जैसनऽ नदी के स्रोत के पता लगाय लेलकै । ई कैलाशक प्राचीन वर्णनसँ मेल खाइत छल जे नदीक जन्म दैत अछि , आ तेँ पहिचान अटकि गेल ।

19म शताब्दी धरि भारत आ नेपाल सं तीर्थयात्री लोकनिक छोट मुदा स्थिर प्रवाह होइत छल, जे प्रायः हिमालयी दर्रा पार करयवला व्यापारिक कारवां के बगल में छल.

एकटा तीर्थयात्रा बंद भ गेल आ फेर खुजल

1950 में चीन के तिब्बत पर नियंत्रण के पुष्टि के बाद चीन आ भारत 1954 के समझौता में आधिकारिक तीर्थ मार्ग के बातचीत केलक। ओ व्यवस्था बेसी दिन नहि चलल। 1959 में चीनी शासनक विरुद्ध तिब्बती विद्रोह दबा देल गेल, आ दलाई लामा – तिब्बती बौद्ध धर्मक आध्यात्मिक नेता – भारत भागि गेलाह ; तिब्बत के भीतर धार्मिक जीवन पर बाद के साल में बहुत प्रतिबंध लगा देल गेल छल | 1962 मे भारत आ चीन अपन विवादित सीमा पर युद्ध लड़ल छल, जकर बाद लगभग दू दशक धरि सीमा भारतीय तीर्थयात्री लेल बंद भ गेल।

1981 में मार्ग फेर सं खुजल, आ तिब्बती लोकनि कें सेहो तीर्थयात्रा फेर सं शुरू करबाक अनुमति भेटल. मुदा तहिया सं बहुतो तिब्बती लोकनि कें आवश्यक परमिट लेबय में दिक्कत भेलनि, आ दोसर लोकनि कैलाश में होटल आ सड़कक बेसी निर्माणक आलोचना केलनि.

आइ अधिकांश तीर्थयात्री निजी टूर कंपनी क संग यात्रा करैत छथि। एहि साल मांग चीनी सरकार के भारतीय तीर्थयात्री के लेल 24 हजार परमिट के कोटा सं काफी ऊपर छल. भारत सरकार आधिकारिक तीर्थयात्रा के प्रायोजक सेहो करैत अछि, जाहि मे भाग लेबय वाला के लॉटरी सं चुनल जाइत अछि, मुदा जगह 1000 लोक तक सीमित अछि. कोविड-19 आरू गलवान घाटी म॑ अखनी तलक विवादित भारत-चीन सीमा प॑ भारतीय आरू चीनी सैनिकऽ के बीच जानलेवा झड़प के वजह स॑ २०२० स॑ बंद होय के बाद ही भारतीय यात्री सिनी के तीर्थयात्रा २०२५ म॑ ही शुरू होय गेलऽ छेलै ।

आइ कैलाश के इतिहास के कोनो बिन्दु स बेसी तीर्थयात्री भेटैत अछि । भारत स॑ अधिकांश यात्री अब॑ काठमांडू लेली उड़ान भर॑ छै आरू बस स॑ नेपाल आरू तिब्बत के बीच एगो सड़क क्रासिंग ग्यिरॉंग के माध्यम स॑ आगू बढ़ै छै जेकरऽ विस्तार २०१४ म॑ करलऽ गेलै आरू २०१७ म॑ अंतरराष्ट्रीय यात्री लेली खुललऽ छेलै ।२०१५ के भूकंप न॑ मुख्य विकल्प क॑ नुकसान पहुँचैला के बाद ई सबसें लोकप्रिय मार्ग बनी गेलै । इएह क्रासिंग छल जे 26 अगस्त क बाढ़ि नष्ट क देलक।

full_article:
Vasundhara Unnava and Hanumantha Rao Unnava are among the people missing. Courtesy Smitha Magal

The former dean of UC Davis Graduate School of Management and his wife are among the thousands of people missing following last week’s flash floods at the Nepal-China border.

Hanumantha Rao Unnava had recently retired from his position as dean when he decided to go on a holiday to Nepal and Tibet with his wife Vasundhara, who lectures at UC Davis, according to their daughter Vaasavi Unnava.

The couple, who are US citizens, had described the holiday as a “trip of a lifetime,” Vaasavi told CNN. “The plan was to cross the border from Nepal into Tibet the day that the floods hit.”

When Vaasavi heard about the disaster last week, she texted her father but the message failed to deliver. “That’s when I realized something was really wrong,” she said.

Despite her best efforts, Vaasavi has been unable to make contact with her parents, or receive any information on their condition.

“The Nepali president went on the news and he said a lot of the survivors are being held in this area called Dhunche, that does not have cell service,” Vaasavi said. “But it’s been six days, and so like the fact that no government in the world has been trying to make sure that coverage is getting there, so we can also ping survivor cell phones, is really disconcerting.”

After learning that the Nepali police have been asking families of loved ones to provide DNA samples to help identify people, Vaasavi called the US State Department to ask them about the protocol.

“The person on the other end of the line said that they didn’t know that the Nepali police had actually said that,” Vaasavi said.

In the meantime, all Vaasavi can do is plead for more information. “We have no idea like where the [rescue] operations are even going on,” Vaasavi said. “My parents were kind of in the epicenter where everything really went wrong in Nepal.”

नेपाल-चीन सीमा पर पिछला सप्ताह आयल आकस्मिक बाढ़ि के बाद लापता हजारों लोक मे यूसी डेविस ग्रेजुएट स्कूल ऑफ मैनेजमेंट के पूर्व डीन आओर हुनकर पत्नी सेहो शामिल छथिन्ह.

हनुमंत राव उन्नावा हालहि मे डीन पद स सेवानिवृत्त भ गेल छलाह जखन ओ अपन पत्नी वसुंधरा क संग नेपाल आ तिब्बत मे छुट्टी मनाबय लेल जेबाक फैसला केलथि जे यूसी डेविस मे व्याख्यान दैत छथि, हुनकर बेटी वासवी उन्नावा क अनुसार।

वासवी न॑ सीएनएन क॑ बतैलकै कि अमेरिकी नागरिक ई जोड़ी न॑ ई छुट्टी क॑ “जीवन भर के यात्रा” बतैन॑ छेलै । “योजना छल जे जाहि दिन बाढ़ि आबि जायत ओहि दिन नेपाल सँ सीमा पार क’ तिब्बत मे प्रवेश कयल जाय।”

पिछला सप्ताह जखन वासवी एहि आपदा के बारे मे सुनलखिन्ह त ओ अपन पिता के मेसेज केलखिन्ह मुदा मैसेज नहि पहुंच सकल. ओ बजलीह, “तखन हमरा बुझायल जे सचमुच किछु गड़बड़ भ’ गेल अछि.”

अपनऽ बहुत प्रयास के बावजूद वासवी अपनऽ माता-पिता स॑ संपर्क नै करी सकलऽ छै, नै ही हुनकऽ हालत के बारे म॑ कोय जानकारी नै मिल॑ सकलऽ छै ।

वासवी कहलनि जे, नेपाली राष्ट्रपति समाचार पर गेलाह आ ओ कहलनि जे बहुत रास बचि गेल लोक के धुन्चे नामक एहि इलाका मे राखल गेल अछि, जाहि मे सेल सेवा नहि अछि। “मुदा छह दिन भ’ गेलै, आ तें जेना ई तथ्य जे दुनियाक कोनो सरकार ई सुनिश्चित करबाक प्रयास नहि क’ रहल अछि जे कवरेज ओतय पहुँचि रहल अछि, जाहि सँ हम सब सरवाइवर सेल फोन केँ सेहो पिंग क’ सकब, सचमुच बेचैन करय बला बात अछि.”

नेपाली पुलिस अपन प्रियजन के परिवार स लोक के पहचान करय मे मदद करय लेल डीएनए सैंपल देबय लेल कहैत आबि रहल अछि से पता चलला के बाद वासवी अमेरिकी विदेश विभाग के फोन क प्रोटोकॉल के बारे मे पूछलखिन्ह.

वासावी कहलनि जे, लाइन के दोसर छोर पर बैसल व्यक्ति कहलक जे हमरा सब के ई पता नहि छल जे नेपाली पुलिस वास्तव मे एना कहने छल।

एहि बीच वासवी बस एतबे क सकैत अछि जे बेसी जानकारी क गुहार लगाउ। वासावी कहलनि जे, हमरा सबके एहन कोनो अंदाजा नै अछि जे [बचाव] अभियान कतय तक चलि रहल अछि। “हमर माता-पिता एक तरहेँ ओहि भूकेन्द्र मे छलाह जतय नेपाल मे सचमुच सब किछु गड़बड़ भ’ गेल छल।”

Nepal Flash Floods: Five Days After the Floods, Secondary Health Risks Rise

By Lara Cooper

Five days have passed since flash floods and debris flows swept through the border region of northern Nepal, and emergency responders are continuing search and rescue efforts, including for several hundred workers believed to be trapped in underground tunnels near hydropower projects in the area.

The death toll rose to 950 people on Monday, with more than 4,400 people missing. Access remains extremely limited, with 32 bridges destroyed and 25 miles of road destroyed. Many places are only reachable by helicopter, and monsoonal rains are threatening to cause further flooding. Roughly 10,000 households need immediate relief, according to Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority.

Direct Relief-supported organizations have deployed to the disaster zone with equipment and medications pre-positioned before the floods began.

Direct Relief partner Dhulikhel Hospital has emergency medical staff on the ground, with a medical team based out of Dhunche, about 12 miles southwest down valley from the main border-crossing impact zone.

The group reported that they have deployed doctors and surgeons via Nepal Army helicopters to bolster the capacity of hospitals in the impacted areas, including Rasuwa Hospital. In addition, Dhulikhel Hospital doctors have flown into Syabrubesi to support internally displaced people, and to Galgung to provide care to hydropower tunnel survivors.

The Transition to Secondary Health Emergency Risks

While search and rescue operations are still underway, the immediate life-saving work is giving way to restoring basic health services for thousands of displaced people, including primary care, medication for diabetes and high blood pressure, care for pregnant women and new mothers, and clean water and hygiene, said Gordon Willcock, Direct Relief’s Asia Pacific Regional Director.

“The concern our partners raise most urgently is disease,” he said. “When people are displaced into crowded conditions without safe water or sanitation, in an environment where human and animal remains have not been recovered, outbreaks become the second emergency. That is why the requests we are receiving are for IV fluids, antibiotics, protective equipment, rapid diagnostic tests, and water treatment supplies.”

On-the-Ground Healthcare Deployment

To support these needs, Direct Relief is preparing a 21-ton shipment of medical aid and medications to multiple organizations in Nepal, including Dhulikhel Hospital and Mountain Heart Nepal, which also deployed to impacted areas to provide care with Direct Relief-donated medical supplies.

Items included in the shipment:

Diabetes management medications and supplies

Respiratory health medicines

Essential medications

Trauma and wound care supplies

Solar chargers and lights

Emergency health kits , filled with medicines and supplies commonly requested after emergencies

, filled with medicines and supplies commonly requested after emergencies Field medic packs , designed for first responders providing care in disaster settings

, designed for first responders providing care in disaster settings Hygiene products, including soap, shampoo, and dental care items for displaced people

Direct Relief has shared its available medical inventory with Nepal’s Ministry of Health and other in-country partners, and is working through formal request lists as they come in â currently weighted toward IV fluids, antibiotics, protective equipment, rapid diagnostic tests, and water treatment supplies.

Direct Relief is also providing financial support to the Shanti Foundation for emergency flood response efforts to impacted women and children. The foundation, led by Shanti Tamang, a long-time partner of Direct Relief, will be providing hygiene supplies, child-friendly spaces in displacement centers and temporary settlements, and psychosocial support.

Long-Term Commitment to Nepal’s Health Infrastructure

Direct Relief’s engagement in Nepal dates to 1985 and has provided more than $119 million in medical aid across 48 partner organizations, 206 shipments, 638,000 lbs. of aid, and 34.9 million defined daily doses of medicine â including a $287,000 shipment of diabetes and cancer medications delivered this month, before the flood.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Direct Relief doing right now in response to the Nepal Floods?

Direct Relief has issued an emergency operating grant to Mountain Heart Nepal and is supporting its emergency medical teams, which are using pre-positioned Direct Relief field medic packs to reach flood-affected communities in Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts. Direct Relief is also coordinating delivery of medicines, medical supplies and hygiene kits to Nepal’s Ministry of Health, and has shared available medical inventory with the Ministry and other in-country partners.

Why does access matter in an emergency?

Because medicines and clinicians only help if they can reach patients. Rasuwa’s mountainous terrain was difficult to access even before the flood; now, with roads, bridges and hydropower infrastructure destroyed, some communities are reachable only by helicopter and moving people and supplies is itself a medical challenge. Supporting transportation, logistics and locally led distribution is central to this response, the same way it has been in prior Direct Relief responses to remote and disaster-damaged terrain.

What will Nepal need most?

Needs typically change over time. The first phase emphasizes trauma care, wound care, surgery and search-and-rescue support, with an unusually large search operation underway across Nuwakot and Rasuwa. As the response progresses, needs can shift toward safe water, infectious disease prevention, mental-health support and uninterrupted treatment for chronic disease and maternal health â particularly in communities cut off by damaged transportation routes.

What experience does Direct Relief have in Nepal?

Direct Relief has supported Nepal’s health system for decades, including the 2015 earthquake response, COVID-19 oxygen infrastructure support, and ongoing outreach to hard-to-reach mountain communities through Mountain Heart Nepal. Those existing relationships matter during emergencies because they provide established channels for communication, assessment and support.

How is this different from the 2015 earthquake response?

They are separate emergencies with different causes and geographies, though both tested Nepal’s mountainous, hard-to-access terrain. One lesson applies to both: health needs arrive in waves, with trauma first and essential services â chronic disease care, maternal health â needed throughout recovery. Direct Relief approaches each response independently while applying lessons from 2015 about locally led action, requested aid and continuity of care.

How can people support the response?

Direct Relief set up a designated Nepal flood response fund. Donations restricted to Nepal floods will be used only for activities related to Nepal.

नेपाल फ़्लैश फ्लड : बाढ़िक पाँच दिन बाद गौण स्वास्थ्य जोखिम बढि गेल

लारा कूपर द्वारा

उत्तरी नेपाल के सीमावर्ती क्षेत्र में आकस्मिक बाढ़ आ मलबा के बहाव के पांच दिन बीत गेल अछि, आ आपातकालीन प्रतिक्रियाकर्ता के खोज आ बचाव के प्रयास जारी अछि, जाहि में इलाका के जलविद्युत परियोजना के पास भूमिगत सुरंग में फंसल मानल जा रहल कई सौ मजदूर के लेल सेहो शामिल अछि।

सोमदिन मृतकक संख्या बढ़ि कए 950 भ गेल अछि, जखन कि 4400 स बेसी लोक लापता अछि। पहुँच अत्यंत सीमित अछि, जाहि मे 32 पुल नष्ट भ गेल अछि आ 25 मील सड़क नष्ट भ गेल अछि। बहुत ठाम केवल हेलीकॉप्टर सं पहुंचल जा सकैत अछि, आ मानसून के बरखा सं आओर बाढ़ि के खतरा अछि. मोटा-मोटी १० हजार घरके तत्काल राहतके आवश्यकता रहल नेपालके राष्ट्रिय आपदा जोखिम न्यूनीकरण तथा प्रबन्धन प्राधिकरणके अनुसार ।

डायरेक्ट रिलीफ समर्थित संगठन बाढ़ि शुरू होबय सं पहिने पूर्व-स्थापित उपकरण आ दवाई के संग आपदा क्षेत्र मे तैनात भ गेल अछि.

डायरेक्ट रिलीफ पार्टनर धुलिखेल अस्पताल में जमीन पर आपातकालीन चिकित्सा कर्मचारी छै, जेकरऽ मेडिकल टीम मुख्य सीमा पार प्रभाव क्षेत्र स॑ लगभग १२ मील दक्षिण-पश्चिम घाटी स॑ नीचें धुंचे स॑ बाहर स्थित छै ।

रसुवा अस्पताल सहित प्रभावित क्षेत्र मे अस्पतालक क्षमता बढेबाक लेल नेपाली सेनाक हेलीकॉप्टर मार्फत चिकित्सक आ सर्जन तैनात केने समूह जानकारी देलक अछि । एकरऽ अलावा धुलिखेल अस्पताल केरऽ डॉक्टर आतंरिक रूप स॑ विस्थापित लोगऽ के सहायता लेली स्याब्रुबेसी म॑ उड़ान भरलऽ छै, आरू जलविद्युत सुरंग स॑ बची क॑ निकलै वाला लोगऽ के देखभाल करै लेली गलगुंग म॑ भी उड़ान भरलऽ छै ।

माध्यमिक स्वास्थ्य आपातकालीन जोखिम मे संक्रमण

डायरेक्ट रिलीफ केरऽ एशिया प्रशांत क्षेत्रीय निदेशक गॉर्डन विलकॉक न॑ कहलकै कि खोज आरू बचाव केरऽ काम अभी भी जारी छै, लेकिन तत्काल जीवन रक्षक काम हजारों विस्थापित लोगऽ लेली बुनियादी स्वास्थ्य सेवा बहाल करै के रास्ता द॑ रहलऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ प्राथमिक देखभाल, मधुमेह आरू उच्च रक्तचाप केरऽ दवाई, गर्भवती महिला आरू नयका मां के देखभाल, आरू स्वच्छ पानी आरू स्वच्छता शामिल छै ।

ओ कहला जे हमर साथी सबस बेसी तत्काल चिंता पैदा करैत छथि ओ अछि बीमारी। "जखन लोग सुरक्षित पानी या स्वच्छता के बिना भीड़भाड़ वाला परिस्थिति में विस्थापित होय जाय छै, ऐन्हऽ वातावरण में जहाँ मानव आरू जानवरऽ के अवशेष नै बरामद होय गेलऽ छै, त॑ प्रकोप दोसरऽ आपातकालीन स्थिति बनी जाय छै । यही वजह छै कि हमरा सब क॑ जे आग्रह मिल॑ लगलऽ छै, वू छै आईवी द्रव, एंटीबायोटिक, सुरक्षा उपकरण, रैपिड डायग्नोस्टिक टेस्ट, आरू पानी के उपचार के आपूर्ति के लेलऽ।"

जमीन पर स्वास्थ्य देखभाल तैनाती

एहि जरूरत कए पूरा करबा लेल डायरेक्ट रिलीफ नेपाल मे धुलिखेल अस्पताल आ माउंटेन हार्ट नेपाल सहित कईटा संस्था कए 21 टन क चिकित्सा सहायता आ दवाई क खेप तैयार क रहल अछि, जे प्रभावित क्षेत्र मे सेहो तैनात अछि ताकि डायरेक्ट रिलीफ दान मे देल गेल चिकित्सा आपूर्ति स देखभाल उपलब्ध कराउल जा सकए।

लदान मे शामिल आइटम:

मधुमेह प्रबंधन दवाई एवं आपूर्ति

श्वसन स्वास्थ्य दवाइयाँ

आघात आ घाव के देखभाल के सामान

सोलर चार्जर आ लाइट

आपातकालीन स्वास्थ्य किट , दवाइयक आ आपूर्ति सं भरल जे आमतौर पर आपातकालीन स्थिति कें बाद मांगल जायत छै

, आपातकालीन स्थितियक कें बाद आमतौर पर अनुरोध कैल गेल दवाइयक आ आपूर्ति सं भरल फील्ड मेडिक पैक , आपदा कें सेटिंग मे देखभाल प्रदान करएय वाला फर्स्ट रिस्पांसर कें लेल डिजाइन कैल गेल छै

, आपदा सेटिंग मे देखभाल प्रदान करएय वाला फर्स्ट रिस्पांसर कें लेल डिजाइन कैल गेल छै स्वच्छता उत्पादक, जइ मे साबुन, शैम्पू, आ विस्थापित लोगक कें लेल दंत देखभाल कें सामान शामिल छै

डायरेक्ट रिलीफ न॑ अपनऽ उपलब्ध चिकित्सा इन्वेंट्री क॑ नेपाल केरऽ स्वास्थ्य मंत्रालय आरू अन्य देशऽ के भीतर के भागीदारऽ के साथ साझा करलकै, आरू औपचारिक अनुरोध सूची के माध्यम स॑ काम करी रहलऽ छै, कैन्हेंकि ई सब आबै छै â वर्तमान म॑ आईवी द्रव, एंटीबायोटिक, सुरक्षा उपकरण, रैपिड डायग्नोस्टिक टेस्ट, आरू जल उपचार आपूर्ति के तरफ भारित छै ।

डायरेक्ट रिलीफ प्रभावित महिला आ बच्चाक कें आपातकालीन बाढ़ प्रतिक्रिया प्रयासक कें लेल शांति फाउंडेशन कें आर्थिक सहायता सेहो द रहल छै. डायरेक्ट रिलीफ केरऽ लंबा समय स॑ भागीदार शांति तामांग के नेतृत्व म॑ बनलऽ ई फाउंडेशन स्वच्छता के सामान, विस्थापन केंद्र आरू अस्थायी बस्ती म॑ बच्चा सिनी के अनुकूल जगह, आरू मनोसामाजिक सहायता उपलब्ध कराबै वाला छै ।

नेपाल के स्वास्थ्य आधारभूत संरचना के प्रति दीर्घकालीन प्रतिबद्धता |

नेपाल मे डायरेक्ट रिलीफ के जुड़ाव 1985 स अछि आ 48 साझेदार संगठन, 206 शिपमेंट, 638,000 पाउंड मे 11.9 करोड़ डॉलर स बेसी के चिकित्सा सहायता उपलब्ध करा चुकल अछि। सहायता केरऽ, आरू 34.9 मिलियन परिभाषित दैनिक खुराक केरऽ दवाई â जेकरा म॑ बाढ़ स॑ पहल॑, ई महीना म॑ डायबिटीज आरू कैंसर केरऽ दवाई केरऽ 287,000 डॉलर के खेप भी शामिल छै ।

नेपाल बाढ़िक प्रतिक्रिया मे अखन डायरेक्ट रिलीफ की क' रहल अछि?

डायरेक्ट रिलीफ न॑ माउंटेन हार्ट नेपाल क॑ आपातकालीन संचालन अनुदान जारी करी क॑ अपनऽ आपातकालीन चिकित्सा टीम क॑ सहयोग करी रहलऽ छै, जे रसुवा आरू नुवाकोट जिला म॑ बाढ़ प्रभावित समुदाय तलक पहुँचै लेली पूर्व-स्थापित डायरेक्ट रिलीफ फील्ड मेडिक पैक के इस्तेमाल करी रहलऽ छै । डायरेक्ट रिलीफ नेपाल के स्वास्थ्य मंत्रालय में दवाई, चिकित्सा आपूर्ति आ स्वच्छता किट के वितरण के समन्वय सेहो क रहल अछि, आ मंत्रालय आ अन्य देश के भीतर के भागीदार के संग उपलब्ध चिकित्सा इन्वेंट्री साझा केलक अछि.

आपातकाल मे पहुंच कें महत्व कियैक होयत छै?

कारण दवाई आ चिकित्सक तखने मदद करैत छथि जखन ओ मरीज तक पहुंचि सकैत छथि। रसुवा’क पहाड़ी इलाका मे बाढ़ि सं पहिने सेहो पहुँचब कठिन छल; आब सड़क, पुल आ जलविद्युत बुनियादी ढांचा नष्ट भ गेल अछि, किछु समुदाय केवल हेलीकॉप्टर सं पहुंचल जा सकैत अछि आ लोक आ आपूर्ति के स्थानांतरित करब स्वयं एकटा चिकित्सा चुनौती अछि. परिवहन, रसद आ स्थानीय नेतृत्व वाला वितरण कें समर्थन करनाय अइ प्रतिक्रिया कें केंद्रीय छै, जेना कि दूरस्थ आ आपदा सं क्षतिग्रस्त इलाकाक पर पूर्व प्रत्यक्ष राहत प्रतिक्रियाक मे भेल छै.

नेपाल के सबसँ बेसी की चाही?

आवश्यकता आमतौर पर समय कें साथ बदलैत छै. पहिलऽ चरण म॑ आघात देखभाल, घाव के देखभाल, सर्जरी आरू खोज-बचाव समर्थन प॑ जोर देलऽ गेलऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ पूरा नुवाकोट आरू रसुवा म॑ असामान्य रूप स॑ बड़ऽ खोज अभियान चलैलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै । जेना-जेना प्रतिक्रिया बढ़यत जायत छै, जरूरतक सुरक्षित जल, संक्रामक रोगक कें रोकथाम, मानसिक-स्वास्थ्य समर्थन आ पुरानी बीमारी आ मातृ स्वास्थ्य कें लेल निर्बाध उपचार कें तरफ बढ़ सकय छै â विशेष रूप सं क्षतिग्रस्त परिवहन मार्गक सं कटल समुदायक मे.

डायरेक्ट रिलीफ के नेपाल मे की अनुभव अछि ?

डायरेक्ट रिलीफ न॑ दशकों स॑ नेपाल केरऽ स्वास्थ्य प्रणाली क॑ सहयोग करी रहलऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ २०१५ केरऽ भूकंप प्रतिक्रिया, कोविड-१९ ऑक्सीजन बुनियादी ढाँचा केरऽ समर्थन, आरू माउंटेन हार्ट नेपाल के माध्यम स॑ मुश्किल स॑ पहुँचै वाला पहाड़ी समुदाय तलक जारी पहुँच शामिल छै । आपातकाल कें दौरान ओ मौजूदा संबंधक कें महत्व होयत छै, कियाकि इ संचार, आकलन आ समर्थन कें लेल स्थापित चैनल प्रदान करएयत छै.

ई सब अलग-अलग आपातकालीन स्थिति छै जेकरऽ कारण आरू भूगोल अलग-अलग छै, हालांकि दोनों नेपाल केरऽ पहाड़ी, मुश्किल स॑ पहुँचै वाला इलाका के परीक्षण करलकै । एकटा पाठ दूनू पर लागू होयत छै: स्वास्थ्य कें जरूरतक लहरक मे पहुंचएयत छै, जइ मे आघात पहिले आ आवश्यक सेवाक â पुरानी बीमारी कें देखभाल, मातृ स्वास्थ्य â पूरा रिकवरी कें दौरान जरूरत छै. प्रत्यक्ष राहत प्रत्येक प्रतिक्रिया कें स्वतंत्र रूप सं संपर्क करयत छै जखन कि स्थानीय रूप सं नेतृत्व कैल गेल कार्यवाही, अनुरोधित सहायता आ देखभाल कें निरंतरता कें बारे मे 2015 सं सबक कें लागू करयत छै.

लोक प्रतिक्रिया के कोना समर्थन क सकैत अछि?

डायरेक्ट रिलीफ नेपाल बाढ़ प्रतिक्रिया कोष निर्धारित कएल गेल । नेपाल बाढ़ि तक सीमित चंदा के उपयोग केवल नेपाल स संबंधित गतिविधि के लेल होयत।

full_article: Rescuers raced Monday to free hundreds of workers believed to be trapped in tunnels at hydropower sites that were buried in mud by catastrophic flooding on the Nepal-China border, as the death toll climbed and increasingly desperate families searched for missing loved ones. The combined deaths in Nepal and China surpassed 950, with more than 4,400 people missing. A private-sector association representing power companies said at least 900 workers were unaccounted for at 12 hydropower projects damaged by the flash floods in Nepal's Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts. About 500 of those workers were believed to be trapped in tunnels. At least one expert said that some workers could have access to oxygen, but others warned that the chances of finding survivors were diminishing. As the rescue efforts intensified, four bodies were recovered from three mud-filled tunnels, Nepal's army said. "I'm not a betting man but I'm an optimist. If there's someone alive, or there's people alive out there, we're doing our best to find them," Arnold Dix, an Australian expert in tunnel rescues, told CBC News from Melbourne on Monday. Dix has been asked to assist in finding survivors at hydro project sites where the buildings have washed away and the tunnels are all that remains. "We know that virtually anyone near the surface or near the entrances to those tunnels have lost their lives," he said, adding that the deaths of workers trapped in tunnels means an "enormous loss" for the country. "Nepal has lost … so many of their experts." Arnold Dix, an Australian expert in tunnel rescues, has been asked to assist in finding survivors at hydro project sites where the buildings have washed away and the tunnels are all that remains. Some workers managed to call for help when the disaster struck last Wednesday, and others who managed to flee reported to authorities and relatives that many of their colleagues were still in the tunnels, said Mohan Kumar Dangi, president of the Independent Power Producers' Association, Nepal (IPPAN.) It was unclear whether rescuers have had any contact with the trapped workers since the initial calls for help. Six days after the disaster, fears were growing that some might have suffocated, Dangi said. Uttam Bhlon Lama, senior vice-president at IPPAN, told CBC's As It Happens Monday that the association is helping the government with rescue operations, providing maps and diagrams of the projects. He said the lack of heavy equipment and sheer inexperience with this level of disaster is daunting, but that no one is prepared to give up and assume the workers are lost. "We are still hopeful because until and unless we don't reach there, we don't see it," he told host Nil Köksal. "They're our loved ones. So we cannot trust that they're no more." Uttam Bhlon Lama, senior vice-president of the Independent Power Producers' Association, spoke to As It Happens host Nil Kӧksal. Built to control water flow Rescue efforts were focused on people trapped in the gigantic tunnels built for controlling the flow of water. "These tunnels are big enough to drive trucks through," said Jakob Steiner, a geoscientist at the University of Graz in Austria based in Dhaka, Bangladesh. "And from what we understand, they have managed to get oxygen to some of those stuck inside and are trying to rescue them now. It's a race for time, though, as people need food and water." In the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project, in the hard-hit Rasuwa district, at least 576 people were missing, Dangi said, adding that around 300 of them were believed to be trapped inside the project's tunnel. At the Trishuli-3 Hydropower Project, crews were working to descend about 15 metres into a tunnel in an effort to reach those believed trapped inside, according to Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet, Nepal's army spokesman. Workers shovelling mud from a flood-ravaged power station in Dhading, Nepal, told The Associated Press that the station is a key connection for providing power to over 20,000 people in the region. PHOTOS | Satellite images of devastation: China rebuilding road On the Chinese side, rescue and recovery efforts included rebuilding the road leading to the Gyirong Port border crossing that regulated travel between China and Nepal. Trucks carried giant rocks as workers tried to repave a portion of the road, state broadcaster CCTV showed Monday, next to rapidly rushing waters, which have been made more powerful by days of rain. The road is now under two to three metres of water. The repaving effort was just a little over a kilometre from the border, CCTV said. Although some rescue teams have managed to reach the border, that represented only a portion of the force. Chinese state media coverage has focused largely on the official response, highlighting the deployment of firefighters, the People's Liberation Army and instructions from top leaders. Little is known about victims on the Chinese side. A rescuer works at the entrance of a tunnel at Chilime Hydropower Plant on Saturday as rescue operations continue for people trapped inside following deadly flash floods and a mudslide, in Rasuwa, Nepal. (Ashish Gurung/Reuters) Canadians still missing Nepal's disaster agency said Monday that 939 deaths had been counted in that country, with 3,925 people missing, including 592 foreigners. As of Sunday, Chinese authorities reported 16 deaths and 546 missing. Chinese state media said 261 of the missing were foreigners, including over 100 Nepalis. There are about 30 Canadians still unaccounted for, according to Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand. Rama Raina's husband, Gireesh, was part of a group making a pilgrimage to Mount Kailash. She told CBC's Andrew Nichols that even though she has not heard from her husband since Aug. 26, she is confident he is alive. "I'm very positive he is safe somewhere," she said Monday from Guelph, Ont. Raina says she knows he was at the Chinese Immigration Centre when the flash flood hit. "This is my firm belief that they are stranded there and waiting for some help," she said, adding that she is frustrated by the lack of information. "But he's definitely somewhere trying to survive and trying to reach [us]," she said. Canada now has ten officials in Kathmandu, including an RCMP officer and the deputy high commissioner of Canada to India to assist in the response, according to Anand. "Canadian officials are working closely with Nepalese and Chinese counterparts, as well as international partners including the Five Eyes, France, Japan, Italy and Singapore, to share information and support efforts to locate and assist Canadians, she said in a statement posted Monday to X. "Officials remain in direct contact with affected families through designated points of contact, are listening to their concerns and suggestions, and will continue to provide updates as information becomes available," Anand said. He visited rescue centers and morgues and went as far as 40 kilometres from where his son was believed to have been, but found no sign of him. His son, Sathya Narayan, had been leading a group of 49 Indian travellers who were returning from Mount Kailash — a sacred site in southwestern Tibet. The group has been missing since floodwaters swept through a Chinese immigration complex where they were waiting to cross into Nepal. Relatives mourn as they repay their respects to Sundari Shrestha, 41, a victim of the flash floods, during her final rites at a crematorium in Kathmandu on Monday. (Monika Malla/Reuters) Nagappan, who owns the Chennai-based travel company that organized the pilgrimage, said the group had been expected to complete immigration formalities and leave for Nepal within about two hours. Instead of making the crossing, they were caught in the flood, Nagappan said. The pilgrimage began Aug. 14. "I haven't heard from my son since then. I don't know whether he is alive or dead," he said. Nagappan said some of those seen fleeing were members of his son's group and were identified by the clothes they were wearing. Wednesday's flash floods started after a glacial collapse high in the Himalayan region. Scientists who studied satellite images said bedrock underneath a glacier high in the Himalayan region had collapsed, taking part of the glacier with it. The rockfall was so extreme that it registered as a magnitude 5.2 seismic event. The rocks and melted water then swelled the rivers in the valleys below, causing a torrent of water that swept buildings, bridges and earth downstream in Tibet and Nepal.

title: Catholic aid worker in Nepal sees ‘long road’ to recovery after ‘unprecedented’ disaster for region - OSV News

full_article:
(OSV News) — Devastation from Aug. 26 flooding and mudslides along the Nepal-China border is staggering, and the road to recovery will be long, a Catholic aid worker now on the ground in that nation told OSV News.

“What we are actually witnessing is unprecedented in these areas,” said Senthil Kumar Gurunathan of Catholic Relief Services, the U.S. bishops’ official humanitarian and development agency.

Gurunathan, CRS country representative for India, spoke with OSV News by phone from Kathmandu hours after landing in Nepal’s capital to assist Caritas Nepal in responding to the disaster. CRS and Caritas Nepal are part of Caritas Internationalis, the Catholic Church’s global humanitarian agency network.

Thousands missing or killed

At least 955 people have been killed and over 4,470 remain missing following an Aug. 26 glacial collapse in Nepal’s Langtang National Park. Debris from the 5.2 magnitude event flowed more than 60 miles, resulting in what the U.S. Geological Survey called “catastrophic impacts downstream” in communities along the Trishuli and Bhote Koshi rivers.

Video and photographs from the region show rapid surges of water and mud churning through the river channels, sweeping away communities. Victims — many of them part of tour groups and Hindu pilgrimages — include hundreds of foreign nationals from some 32 nations, with some 85 Americans still missing.

Determining the number of casualties has been further complicated by the Chinese government’s information restrictions in China and Tibet, which preclude access by foreign journalists.

In his Aug. 30 Angelus address, Pope Leo XIV offered continued “prayers for those affected by the terrible flood that struck Nepal and Tibet.

“Let us pray for those who have lost their lives, for the injured, those missing, for the families and rescue workers,” said Pope Leo. “May the concern of everyone help to alleviate the suffering and provide the necessary aid to the people affected.”

CRS focused on pressing needs

Gurunathan said that “villages and towns have been washed away,” and that “the flood situation and the damage is still evolving.”

“We are very focused on the pressing needs, the essential needs,” which are “food, water, sanitation and shelter,” said Gurunathan.

Getting such aid to those impacted by the disaster is a challenge, he admitted.

“Many of the main roads have been washed away, either fully or partly,” Gurunathan said. “So what we are trying to do is to find alternative routes, working with local people to see what are the existing motorable roads. These may not be the main roads, but these are lifesaving roads, still intact.”

Gurunathan, whose agency has launched a donation campaign for relief efforts, said his team is “also closely coordinating with the government” to “see how we can airlift some of the relief material to those areas which are completely cut off, and where there isn’t a road connection.”

The agency is also committed to addressing the trauma inflicted by the disaster, said Gurunathan.

“Focusing on mental health is going to be a key priority for us moving forward,” as part of a “coordinated effort” with the Nepalese government, he said.

“It’s going to be a long road for recovery,” said Gurunathan. “So I think it’s going to be important to actually express solidarity with the people affected in Nepal, and see how we can help them rebuild their lives.”
