title: Smell of death hangs over rescue efforts in Nepal as deaths pass 1,000 - NBC News
description: Smell of death hangs over rescue efforts in Nepal as deaths pass 1,000  NBC News
publisher.title: NBC News
full_article:
BIDUR, Nepal — The overwhelming stench of death is crushing hopes that more survivors will be found in this Nepalese town devastated by last week’s catastrophic floods.

Workers in white hazmat suits unload bodies from a stream of ambulances in Bidur, a town in Nepal’s Nuwakot district on Tuesday. They place the wrapped bodies onto blue tarp in a cordoned off area.

Helicopters, both military and civilian aircraft that in better days would be used for commercial tours, take off packed with aid before returning with survivors in need of medical care.

Kalpana Shrestha, a nurse who works in capital Kathmandu, is desperate. Ten members of her family are missing — her two sisters and their children — are missing.

Kalpana Shrestha. Adam Galica / NBC News

“I have shared their photos with journalists, on social media and YouTube but I have not got any response at all,” she said speaking with NBC News in Kathmandu. She added that her loved ones disappeared in Betrawati, a town some 60 miles from the capital that was obliterated in the flooding.

“I have posted so much that my fingers started shaking and trembling,” said Shrestha, 35. “My mind has stopped working. But even so, we have not stopped posting.”

More than 1,000 have been declared dead in Nepal after last week’s devastating floods, according to Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority. Over 3,915 others are still missing, including at least 583 foreign nationals. In Tibet, at least 16 people were killed and 546 are missing, according to CGTN, China’s English-language satellite news channel.

At least 80 Americans are among the missing in Nepal.

More than 10,000 people have been rescued so far, including 252 foreign nationals, the United Nations says.

The disaster, which was triggered by a glacier collapse and landslide on Nepal’s border with China, is now considered Nepal’s deadliest natural disaster since the April 2015 earthquake that killed around 9,000 people in Nepal.

A poster featuring Kalpona Shrestha’s missing family members. Adam Galica / NBC News

Shrestha said she felt that the government was “not doing enough work to search and rescue to locate” her family. She also noted that access to her village was still difficult after the floods.

“Our brothers did try but failed to reach them and had to return home,” she said. “The road is gone, there is no access at all.”

Access remains the single biggest obstacle to response efforts, with roads passable only as far as Nuwakot and some sections of highway linking Kathmandu to the hardest areas still completely blocked, according to the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs.

And the bodies that have been recovered pose a huge challenge to authorities, who are using at least 21 hospitals in a string of districts to store remains, according to Nepal’s disaster agency. In some cases, bodies are being buried to prevent any risk of infection, with hopes they will be later identified so the remains can be returned to loved ones.

A health worker sprays disinfectant following flash floods in Devighat on Monday. Arun Sankar / AFP via Getty Images

Speaking with NBC News in Pokhara, Nabin Karki, a superintendent of police, said authorities were collecting DNA samples and display photos of the bodies found so in hopes that family members might be able to identify them.

Relatives of those missing can provide blood samples for DNA testing, he said, and if a match is found the body can be taken from the burial site and handed over to the family for a funeral.

Updated: 7:01 AM EDT Sep 1, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ By SHRISTI KAFLE and SHEIKH SAALIQ, Associated Press

Rescue teams with search dogs combed through mud, rocks and debris Tuesday in Nepal and China, looking for thousands of people still missing after catastrophic flooding tore through communities across the Himalayas, leaving more than 1,000 dead.

Nepal's disaster agency said Tuesday that 987 deaths had been counted there, with 3,916 people missing, including 583 foreigners. Chinese authorities, in their latest update on Sunday, reported 16 deaths and 546 people still missing, including 261 foreigners.

The scale of last week's disaster was hampering rescue efforts in both regions, with landslides, destroyed roads and widespread damage cutting off remote areas. Crews faced challenging conditions as they searched unstable terrain and piles of debris, raising fears the death toll could rise as rescuers reach isolated communities.

Rescuers race to reach missing hydropower workers

In Nepal, rescuers were racing to reach hundreds of workers believed to be trapped inside tunnels at hydropower projects damaged by the floods. About 900 workers are missing from 12 projects, with roughly 500 believed to be trapped in tunnels, according to Nepalese authorities.

Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet, Nepal's army spokesperson, said teams assisted by foreign experts were working at several hydropower projects. Visuals released by the army showed rescue teams entering dark, debris-filled tunnels, wading through mud and water and climbing over rocks as they searched for signs of life.

On the Chinese side, rescue crews scoured areas hit by mudslides, particularly around the Gyirong Port border crossing, which was destroyed.

Some rescuers, aided by search dogs, searched gaps among rocks and debris for signs of life. Other teams used heavy machinery to clear a major highway leading to Gyirong Port, hoping to clear the way for equipment, personnel and supplies to reach the disaster zone, according to China's state-run Global Times newspaper.

Relief operations expand to reach stranded communities

At least 11,814 people have been rescued so far, according to Nepalese authorities. Emergency crews were using helicopters and other aircraft to reach stranded communities in areas where roads and bridges have been destroyed by the flooding and landslides.

Authorities on Tuesday also stepped up efforts to provide assistance to survivors in areas where roads and other transportation routes had been damaged or cut off.

Satellite images show bedrock and glacier collapsed on Nepal-China border, then rivers flooded

Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said China's second batch of relief supplies for Nepal was expected to ship Tuesday, including drones, DNA testing and water purification equipment. Chinese DNA testing experts will also help Nepal identify bodies, he said.

Bimal Sharma, a helicopter pilot who has been flying rescue and relief missions since the disaster began, said he was shocked to see the devastation in Timure, a border town close to Tibet that he has known for years.

"It felt like I was flying over an entirely different landscape," he said.

Sharma said he has had little opportunity to speak with the people he rescued, but their expressions told him how deeply the disaster had affected them.

"I can see the pain in their eyes. It's heartbreaking," he said.

The disaster began with a glacial collapse high in the Himalayas

The Aug. 26 disaster began with a chain of events high in the Himalayas. A glacial collapse sent large amounts of rock, ice and meltwater into valleys below, triggering powerful floods downstream.

Scientists studying satellite imagery said the collapse appears to have involved the failure of bedrock beneath a glacier in the Himalayan region. The rockfall was powerful enough to register as a magnitude 5.2 seismic event.

The resulting surge of water and debris entered rivers that flow through valleys in Tibet and Nepal, causing them to rise rapidly. Floodwaters swept away homes, buildings, roads and bridges and carried mud and rocks downstream.

Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah said that the disaster highlighted the need for action to combat climate change.

"This incident has indicated that the risks we face in the Himalayan region are increasing with climate change," Shah said in a social media post Monday night. "Therefore, this region must be alert, and at the same time, it is time for us to strongly raise the issue of disasters caused by climate change before the international community."

लापता जलविद्युत मजदूर तक पहुंचबाक लेल बचावकर्मी दौड़ैत अछि

नेपालमे बाढ़िसँ क्षतिग्रस्त जलविद्युत परियोजनामे सुरंगक भीतर फँसल सैकड़ों मजदूर लग पहुँचबाक लेल बचावकर्मी दौड़ल छल । नेपाली अधिकारी के अनुसार १२ परियोजना स करीब ९०० मजदूर लापता अछि, जाहि मे लगभग ५०० मजदूर सुरंग मे फंसल हेबाक आशंका अछि।

ब्रिगेडियर एस. नेपालके सेनाके प्रवक्ता जनरल राजा राम बस्नेट विदेशी विशेषज्ञके सहयोगमे टोली अनेक जलविद्युत परियोजनामे कार्यरत बतौलनि । सेना द्वारा जारी विजुअल में बचाव दल अन्हार, मलबा स भरल सुरंग में प्रवेश करैत, कीचड़ आ पानि में डुबकी लगाबैत आ चट्टान के ऊपर चढ़ैत देखल गेल अछि, जखन कि ओ जीवन के संकेत खोजैत छल।

चीनी तरफ स॑ बचाव दल न॑ कीचड़ स॑ टकराबै वाला इलाका खास करी क॑ ग्यिरॉंग बंदरगाह सीमा क्रासिंग के आसपास, जे नष्ट होय गेलऽ छेलै ।

खोज कुत्ता के मदद सं किछ बचावकर्मी चट्टान आओर मलबा के बीच के फाँक के तलाशी लेलखिन्ह जेहि सं जीवन के संकेत मिलत. चीन केरऽ सरकारी अखबार ग्लोबल टाइम्स के अनुसार, अन्य टीम न॑ भारी मशीनरी के इस्तेमाल करी क॑ ग्योरॉंग बंदरगाह जाय वाला एगो बड़ऽ राजमार्ग क॑ खाली करै के कोशिश करलकै, जेकरा स॑ ई उम्मीद छेलै कि आपदा क्षेत्र म॑ पहुँचै के रास्ता साफ होय जैतै ।

राहत अभियान फंसल समुदायक तइक पहुंचय कें लेल विस्तार करयत छै

नेपाली अधिकारीसबके अनुसार अखनधरि ११ हजार ८१४ गोटेके उद्धार भेल अछि । आपातकालीन दल हेलीकॉप्टर आरू अन्य विमान के इस्तेमाल करी क॑ वू इलाका म॑ फंसलऽ समुदाय तलक पहुँची रहलऽ छेलै, जहां बाढ़ आरू भूस्खलन स॑ सड़क आरू पुल नष्ट होय गेलऽ छै ।

मंगलवार क॑ अधिकारियऽ न॑ वू इलाका म॑ बची क॑ निकलै वाला लोगऽ क॑ सहायता दै के कोशिश भी तेज करी देलकै, जहां सड़क आरू अन्य परिवहन मार्ग क॑ नुकसान पहुँचलऽ छै या कटलऽ छै ।

उपग्रहक तस्वीर मे नेपाल-चीन सीमा पर बेडरोक आ ग्लेशियर खसि पड़ल, फेर नदी मे बाढ़ि आबि गेल

चीन के विदेश मंत्रालय के प्रवक्ता गुओ जियाकुन कहलनि जे, चीन के नेपाल के लेल राहत के दोसर बैच मंगलदिन भेजय के उम्मीद अछि, जाहि मे ड्रोन, डीएनए परीक्षण आ जल शुद्धिकरण उपकरण शामिल अछि। चीनी डीएनए परीक्षण विशेषज्ञ नेपाल के शव के पहचान करय मे सेहो मदद करत ओ कहलनि।

आपदा शुरू होला के बाद स॑ ही बचाव आरू राहत मिशन उड़ाबै वाला हेलीकॉप्टर पायलट बिमल शर्मा न॑ कहलकै कि तिब्बत केरऽ नजदीकी सीमावर्ती शहर तिमुरे म॑ तबाही देखी क॑ ओकरा चौंक गेलै जेकरा क॑ हुनी सालौ स॑ जानत॑ छै ।

ओ कहला जे एहन लागल जेना हम एकदम अलग परिदृश्य पर उड़ि रहल छी।

शर्मा कहलनि जे, हुनका द्वारा बचाओल गेल लोक सं बात करबाक मौका कम भेटल अछि, मुदा हुनकर भाव सं पता चलैत अछि जे एहि आपदा सं हुनका कतेक गहींर असर पड़ल अछि.

ओ कहलनि जे, हुनका लोकनिक आँखि मे दर्द देखबा मे आबि रहल अछि, ई हृदयविदारक अछि।

आपदा के शुरुआत हिमालय के ऊँचाई पर हिमनदी के पतन स॑ भेलै

26 अगस्त के आपदा के शुरुआत हिमालय में ऊँच घटनाक्रम के श्रृंखला सं भेल छल. हिमनदी केरऽ पतन स॑ भारी मात्रा म॑ चट्टान, बर्फ आरू पिघललऽ पानी नीचें घाटी म॑ भेजलऽ गेलै, जेकरा स॑ नीचें के तरफ शक्तिशाली बाढ़ आबी गेलै ।

उपग्रह केरऽ इमेजरी के अध्ययन करै वाला वैज्ञानिकऽ न॑ कहलकै कि ई पतन म॑ हिमालयी क्षेत्र केरऽ एगो ग्लेशियर के नीचें बेडरोक केरऽ विफलता शामिल नजर आबी रहलऽ छै । ई चट्टान केरऽ गिरना एतना शक्तिशाली छेलै कि ५.२ परिमाण के भूकंपीय घटना के रूप म॑ पंजीकृत होय गेलै ।

एकरऽ परिणामस्वरूप पानी आरू मलबा केरऽ उफान तिब्बत आरू नेपाल केरऽ घाटी स॑ बहय वाला नदी म॑ प्रवेश करी क॑ तेजी स॑ बढ़ी गेलै । बाढ़िक पानि घर, भवन, सड़क आ पुल कए बहरा गेल आ थाल-कादो आ चट्टान कए नीचा ल गेल।

नेपालके प्रधानमन्त्री बलेन्द्र शाह विपदा जलवायु परिवर्तनके निवारणके लेल कार्यवाहीके आवश्यकताके उजागर करल बटैलै ।

सोमदिन राति सोशल मीडिया पोस्ट मे शाह कहलनि जे, ई घटना संकेत देलक अछि जे जलवायु परिवर्तन के संग हिमालय क्षेत्र मे हमरा सब के सामने जे जोखिम बढ़ि रहल अछि। "अतः ई क्षेत्र क॑ सतर्क रहना चाहियऽ, आरू साथ ही साथ ई समय आबी गेलऽ छै कि हम्में जलवायु परिवर्तन के वजह स॑ पैदा होय वाला आपदा के मुद्दा क॑ अंतरराष्ट्रीय समुदाय के सामने मजबूती स॑ उठाबै ।"

___ २.

सालिक नई दिल्ली स रिपोर्ट केलनि। बीजिंग केरऽ एसोसिएटेड प्रेस केरऽ पत्रकार ई. एडुआर्डो कास्टिलो, हांगकांग केरऽ कनिस लेउंग आरू नई दिल्ली केरऽ ऐजाज हुसैन न॑ ई रिपोर्ट म॑ योगदान देल॑ छै ।

title: American missing in wake of Nepal floods contacted, Nepali officials tell CBS News - CBS News
description: American missing in wake of Nepal floods contacted, Nepali officials tell CBS News  CBS News
publisher.title: CBS News
full_article:
Kathmandu, Nepal — One of the dozens of U.S. nationals missing in the wake of the devastating flash floods on the Nepal-Tibet border has been contacted, Nepali government officials confirmed to CBS News on Tuesday.

About 85 Americans were still listed as missing, and word that rescuers have managed to contact one could bring hope to thousands of families around the world desperately waiting for word of loved ones.

CBS News was still working to confirm details of the case, and it was unclear who the U.S. national contacted by Nepali agencies might be, where they were located or what condition they were in.

More than 4,600 people were still believed to be missing and at least 1,050 confirmed dead in Nepal alone as of Tuesday, authorities said. Chinese authorities have confirmed that 16 people were killed in Tibet, and more than 550 remained missing on that sided of the border.

People scout for usable materials from debris after flash floods at Trishuli Center in Nepal's Nuwakot district, Sept. 1, 2026. Arun SANKAR/AFP/Getty

About 600 hydroelectric power plant workers are among the missing in Nepal, believed to be trapped inside several projects in the disaster area, according to the Himalayan nation's prime minister.

Work by search and rescue teams to clear mud-blocked tunnels to reach the workers has continued apace, amid concern that oxygen inside could run out.

It was almost a week ago that a mountainside and glacier collapse in the Himalayas triggered avalanches in Tibet and Nepal, which in turn triggered the devastating flash floods.

Recovery teams have found bodies in riverbeds far downstream. No one in the region can remember the sacred Trishuli River ever swelling higher than it did last week.

Rohit Tamang, 22, has spent his entire life in his home perched above the Trishuli. He told CBS News he watched helplessly when the waters surged last Wednesday, and he's not leaving now, "because my childhood memories are here."

Nepal's foreign minister told CBS News on Tuesday that authorities believe many foreigners may have been hiking in the mountains when the disaster struck, leaving them marooned without communications, but possibly safe.

He was hopeful that, rather than mud and water, more good news could soon come down from the Himalayas.

काठमांडू, नेपाल : नेपाल-तिब्बत सीमा पर भेल विनाशकारी आकस्मिक बाढ़ि के बाद लापता दर्जनों अमेरिकी नागरिक मे सँ एक सँ संपर्क कयल गेल अछि, नेपाली सरकारक अधिकारी मंगलदिन सीबीएस न्यूज केँ पुष्टि केलनि।

लगभग 85 अमेरिकी क॑ अखनी भी लापता के रूप म॑ सूचीबद्ध करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै, आरू ई खबर कि बचावकर्ता सिनी स॑ संपर्क करै म॑ सफल होय गेलऽ छै, दुनिया भर के हजारों परिवारऽ लेली आशा पैदा करी सकै छै जे अपनऽ प्रियजनऽ के खबर के बेताब इंतजार करी रहलऽ छै ।

सीबीएस न्यूज एखनहु एहि मामलाक विवरणक पुष्टि करबा मे लागल छल, आ ई स्पष्ट नहि छल जे नेपाली एजेंसी द्वारा संपर्क कयल गेल अमेरिकी नागरिक के भ' सकैत अछि, ओ कतय छथि वा कोन हालत मे छथि.

अखनो 4600 स बेसी लोक के लापता हेबाक आशंका अछि आ मंगलदिन धरि असगर नेपाल मे कम स कम 1050 के मौत के पुष्टि भेल अधिकारी सब कहलनि। चीनी अधिकारी न॑ ई बात के पुष्टि करलकै कि तिब्बत म॑ १६ लोगऽ के मौत होय गेलऽ छै, आरू सीमा केरऽ वू तरफ ५५० स॑ भी अधिक लोग लापता छै ।

नेपाल के नुवाकोट जिला के त्रिशुली केन्द्र मे आकस्मिक बाढ़ के बाद मलबा स उपयोगी सामग्री के लेल लोक स्काउट करैत छथि, 1 सितम्बर 2026. अरुण संकर/एएफपी/गेटी

नेपाल मे लापता मे लगभग 600 जलविद्युत संयंत्रक मजदूर शामिल अछि, जकरा आपदा क्षेत्र मे कतेको परियोजना के भीतर फंसल मानल जा रहल अछि, हिमालय राष्ट्र के प्रधानमंत्री के अनुसार।

मजदूरऽ तक पहुँचै लेली कीचड़ स॑ बंद सुरंगऽ क॑ साफ करै के खोज आरू बचाव टीमऽ के काम तेजी स॑ जारी छै, ई चिंता के बीच कि भीतर के ऑक्सीजन खतम होय सकै छै ।

लगभग एक सप्ताह पहिने के बात छै कि हिमालय में पहाड़ के ढाल आरू ग्लेशियर के गिरला के बाद तिब्बत आरू नेपाल में हिमस्खलन शुरू होय गेलै, जेकरा चलतें विनाशकारी आकस्मिक बाढ़ के शुरुआत होय गेलै ।

रिकवरी टीम कए नदी क बहुत नीचा नदी क तल मे लाश भेटल अछि। एहि क्षेत्र मे कियो याद नहि क सकैत अछि जे पवित्र त्रिशुली नदी कहियो पिछला सप्ताह स बेसी सूजन भेल छल।

NEW DELHI (AP) — Rescue crews in Nepal are racing against time to find hundreds of missing workers who are feared trapped inside hydropower tunnels damaged by flooding that has killed more than 1,000 people across Nepal and China.

At least 900 workers are missing from hydropower projects, with about 500 believed to be inside tunnels, according to officials and industry representatives.

Other WRAL Top Stories

Access to the tunnels has been hampered by flooding, debris and damaged infrastructure, making it difficult for rescue teams to reach workers.

Rescuers are scouring tunnels filled with debris

Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet, a Nepal Army spokesperson, said teams assisted by foreign experts were working at several hydropower projects. Army footage showed rescuers entering dark, debris-filled tunnels, wading through mud and climbing over rocks as they searched for the missing.

Mohan Kumar Dangi, president of the Independent Power Producers Association of Nepal, said floods damaged at least 12 hydropower projects in Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts, with a combined capacity of 670 MW. Four were under construction, seven operational and one in testing phase, he said.

Hydropower projects undergo risk assessments and other studies before construction, but called the Aug. 26 flooding “something unimaginable,” Dangi said.

Flood damage is hampering access to tunnels

The biggest challenge for rescuers is reaching them.

Many of Nepal’s hydropower projects are in remote, mountainous areas where steep terrain and narrow roads can make access difficult. Flooding has worsened conditions, damaging roads and limiting routes to some sites.

Rescuers also are facing tunnels that are blocked or damaged.

The floods swept mud, huge rocks and debris into underground passages, collapsing sections and trapping workers. Even where tunnel entrances are accessible, crews must clear large amounts of debris before reaching deeper sections.

Debris is obscuring the locations of workers

Finding the missing workers also has proved difficult.

Filmmaker and drone pilot Manish Maharjan, who has been volunteering with the Nepalese army, said some tunnels were “filled with mud like toothpaste in a tube.” At one hydropower project, he used a drone to search to the end of a tunnel but found no sign of life.

Some workers called for help during early hours after floods, while others who escaped said colleagues remained underground. It was not clear whether rescuers had since made contact with those workers or whether they were still alive.

Experts say the first 72 hours after a disaster can be critical. People trapped underground may survive without food for some time, but limited drinking water and breathable air can quickly become life-threatening.

Nepal’s rescue capacity is being tested

Anil Pokhrel, a disaster risk reduction expert and former head of Nepal’s disaster authority, said the flooding exposed weaknesses in Nepal’s rescue capacity. He said rescuers lost valuable time locating the tunnel’s exact entry point and coordinates and lacked heavy equipment and adequately trained personnel.

“Harsh and remote locations with inclement weather worsened the situation. Also, we didn’t have adequately trained human resources to undertake such operations,” he said.

Nepal has more than a century of experience building tunnels but remains poorly prepared for complex tunnel rescues, Pokhrel said.

“We are focused on tunnel design and construction but are not adequately prepared for rescue operations,” he said.

——

Kafle reported from Kathmandu, Nepal.

अधिकारी आ उद्योग प्रतिनिधि क अनुसार जलविद्युत परियोजना स कम स कम 900 मजदूर लापता अछि, जाहि मे करीब 500 मजदूर सुरंग क अंदर हेबाक आशंका अछि।

अन्य WRAL शीर्ष कहानियाँ

बाढ़, मलबा आ क्षतिग्रस्त बुनियादी ढांचा के कारण सुरंग तक पहुंच में बाधा आबि गेल अछि, जाहि सं बचाव टीम के मजदूर तक पहुंचनाय मुश्किल भ गेल अछि.

बचावकर्मी मलबा स भरल सुरंग कए झाड़ू लगा रहल अछि

ब्रिगेडियर एस. नेपाली सेनाके प्रवक्ता जनरल राजा राम बस्नेट विदेशी विशेषज्ञके सहयोगमे टोली अनेक जलविद्युत परियोजनामे कार्यरत बतौलनि । सेना केरऽ फुटेज म॑ देखलऽ गेलऽ छै कि बचावकर्मी अन्हार, मलबा स॑ भरलऽ सुरंगऽ म॑ प्रवेश करी क॑ थाल के बीच स॑ डुबकी लगाय क॑ चट्टानऽ प॑ चढ़ी क॑ लापता लोगऽ के खोज करी रहलऽ छै ।

नेपालके स्वतन्त्र विद्युत उत्पादक संघके अध्यक्ष मोहनकुमार डाङी बाढिसँ रसुवा आ नुवाकोट जिल्लामे कमसँ कम १२ जलविद्युत् परियोजनाके क्षति पहुँचल बतौलनि, जकर संयुक्त क्षमता ६७० मेगावाट अछि । ओ कहला जे चारिटा निर्माणाधीन, सातटा परिचालन आ एकटा परीक्षण चरण मे अछि।

डांगी नँ कहलकै कि जलविद्युत परियोजना सिनी मँ निर्माण सँ पहलौ जोखिम के आकलन आरू अन्य अध्ययन करलौ जाय छै, लेकिन 26 अगस्त क बाढ़ क “कुछ अकल्पनीय” कहलकै ।

बाढ़िक नुकसान सुरंग तक पहुंच मे बाधा पहुंचा रहल अछि

बचावकर्ता के लेल सबस पैघ चुनौती हुनका तक पहुंचनाय अछि.

नेपाल केरऽ बहुत सारा जलविद्युत परियोजना दूरस्थ, पहाड़ी क्षेत्रऽ म॑ छै, जहां खड़ा इलाका आरू संकीर्ण सड़कऽ के कारण पहुँच मुश्किल होय सकै छै । बाढ़ि के कारण हालत खराब भ गेल अछि, सड़क के नुकसान पहुंचल अछि आओर किछ जगह पर मार्ग सीमित भ गेल अछि.

बचावकर्मी के सेहो एहन सुरंग के सामना करय पड़ि रहल अछि जे अवरुद्ध या क्षतिग्रस्त भ गेल अछि.

बाढ़ि थाल, विशाल चट्टान आ मलबा भूमिगत मार्ग मे बह गेल, खंड ढहि गेल आ मजदूर फँसा देलक। जहाँ सुरंग के प्रवेश द्वार सुलभ छै, वहीं भी चालक दल क॑ गहरा खंडऽ प॑ पहुँचै स॑ पहल॑ बड़ऽ मात्रा म॑ मलबा साफ करना छै ।

मलबा मजदूर क स्थान अस्पष्ट क रहल अछि

लापता मजदूर के खोजब सेहो मुश्किल साबित भेल अछि.

नेपाली सेना के साथ स्वयंसेवी कार्यरत फिल्म निर्माता आरू ड्रोन पायलट मनीष महर्जन के कहना छै कि कुछ सुरंग “ट्यूब में टूथपेस्ट के तरह कीचड़ स॑ भरलऽ छै ।” एकटा जलविद्युत परियोजना मे ओ ड्रोन क उपयोग कए सुरंग क अंत तक खोजबा लेल केलथि मुदा जीवन क कोनो निशानी नहि भेटल।

बाढ़ि के बाद भोर मे किछ मजदूर मदद के आह्वान केलखिन्ह, त किछ मजदूर जे भागल छलखिन्ह ओ कहलखिन्ह जे सहयोगी भूमिगत रहि गेल छथिन्ह. ई साफ नै छेलै कि ओकरऽ बाद बचावकर्ता सिनी न॑ वू मजदूरऽ स॑ संपर्क करलकै या वू अभी भी जिंदा छै ।

विशेषज्ञ के कहनाय छनि जे कोनो आपदा के बाद पहिल 72 घंटा गंभीर भ सकैत अछि. जमीन कें नीचा फंसल लोग किच्छू समय तइक बिना भोजन कें जीवित रह सकएय छै, मुदा सीमित पीवय कें पानी आ सांस लेवय वाला हवा जल्दी जानलेवा भ सकएय छै.

नेपाल के बचाव क्षमता के परीक्षण भ रहल अछि

आपदा जोखिम कम करय के विशेषज्ञ आ नेपाल के आपदा प्राधिकरण के पूर्व प्रमुख अनिल पोखरेल के कहनाय छनि जे बाढ़ि सं नेपाल के बचाव क्षमता मे कमजोरी के उजागर भेल अछि. हुनी कहलकै कि सुरंग केरौ सटीक प्रवेश बिंदु आरू निर्देशांक के पता लगाबै मँ बचावकर्मी सिनी क बहुमूल्य समय गंवाय देलकै आरू भारी उपकरण आरू पर्याप्त प्रशिक्षित कर्मी के कमी छै ।

ओ कहला जे खराब मौसम क संग कठोर आ दूरस्थ स्थान पर स्थिति आओर खराब भ गेल, संगहि हमरा सब लग एहन ऑपरेशन करबा लेल पर्याप्त प्रशिक्षित मानव संसाधन नहि छल।

नेपाल मे सुरंग बनेबाक एक सदी स बेसी अनुभव अछि, मुदा जटिल सुरंग बचाव क लेल ओ खराब तैयारी मे अछि, पोखरेल कहला।

ओ कहला जे हम सुरंग क डिजाइन आ निर्माण पर ध्यान केंद्रित करि रहल छी, मुदा बचाव कार्य लेल पर्याप्त तैयारी नहि छी।

——

title: Georgia father among thousands missing after catastrophic flooding in Nepal - CBS News
description: Georgia father among thousands missing after catastrophic flooding in Nepal  CBS News
publisher.title: CBS News
full_article:
A Gwinnett County family is holding on to its faith as it awaits word about a father who is among thousands of people unaccounted for after catastrophic flooding and landslides in Nepal.

The humanitarian crisis continues across the Himalayan nation, where the death toll has climbed above 900. More than 4,400 people remain missing, including at least 85 Americans.

Among them is Vivek Srivastav of Suwanee, who was on an eight-day religious pilgrimage to Mount Kailash, a site revered in Hindu tradition as the eternal home of Lord Shiva. Srivastav was traveling with a group of about 10 people when a glacier collapse triggered massive flash flooding near Nepal's border with China. No one in the group has been heard from since.

For his son, Samarth Srivastav, and his wife, Garina, the lack of communication has been devastating.

"I think initially we didn't realize how severe the situation was, but as the hours turned to days and it went longer and longer without hearing anything, it became scarier for us," Samarth said. "We're just in a place where we don't really know anything."

Samarth last spoke with his father Tuesday evening, which was Wednesday morning in Nepal, just hours before the disaster struck.

Critical infrastructure across the region has been severely damaged. Damaged hydropower plants and downed cell towers have cut off electricity, running water and communications. With bridges washed away and mountain passes blocked by heavy mudslides, rescue operations on the ground have stalled, leaving military helicopters as the only way to airlift survivors and deliver emergency supplies.

Vivek Srivastav, who remains unaccounted for after catastrophic flooding in Nepal, attends his son's graduation with his family. CBS News Atlanta

Thousands of miles away, metro Atlanta's Nepalese community is organizing relief efforts. During a recent vigil and fundraiser, community members collected donations for emergency food, medical supplies and aid for children orphaned by the disaster.

"It's very bad. Whole towns, whole cities are gone," said Raju Thapa of the Nepali Cultural Center. "People have lost everything that they have. Any dollar will be helpful for the victims right now."

Even the community's youngest members stepped up, including Thapa's daughter, who donated $51 she earned by selling ice cream.

As specialized rescue teams navigate dangerous terrain to reach isolated pilgrimage trails, the Srivastav family said it is drawing strength from Vivek's resilient and joyful spirit.

"He's just a really fun person to be around. I don't know a single person who does not like him," Samarth said. "He's very levelheaded and steadfast. He's a man of religion. He doesn't care for materialistic things, so I think he's all about living and enjoying life."

"Just keep us in your thoughts and prayers because there's not much else we can do until we hear something," he added.

Local cultural centers and nonprofit aid organizations across metro Atlanta continue to accept donations for medical supplies and food for families affected by the disaster.

title: Nepal flood death toll crosses 1,000 as rescuers reach remote areas - KSL News
description: Nepal flood death toll crosses 1,000 as rescuers reach remote areas  KSL News
publisher.title: KSL News
full_article:
KATHMANDU, Nepal — The death toll in Nepal's flood crossed 1,000 on Tuesday, as rescuers used heavy machinery, helicopters and excavators to reach the thousands still missing, ​nearly a week after the catastrophic Himalayan disaster left a trail of destruction across towns and valleys.

Specialized rescue teams from China, India and Nepal built temporary bridges to reach remote areas and dug through the ruins of hydropower projects in the Himalayas, using excavators to rescue close to 300 workers trapped inside tunnels.

The ‌collapse of a glacier on Aug. 26 sent a deluge of ice, rock and mud sweeping through the impoverished nation's border region with China.

At least 639 people remain stuck in several devastated hydropower stations that have become the ⁠focus of rescue efforts, the country's disaster management authority said on Tuesday.

The total confirmed death ​toll rose to 1,003, with about 4,000 people still missing, including 590 foreign ⁠nationals from 39 countries.

"Thousands of citizens have lost their homes, families, loved ones and property," Prime Minister Balendra Shah said in a late-night social media post on Monday.

Over 11,000 people have ‌been rescued across the affected region, and ‌power and communication lines were restored in some areas, he said, promising support for those who were displaced.

More than 9,200 personnel were deployed in ⁠the affected areas, coordinating the search and rescue of the injured, assisting in the management of bodies, opening blocked ⁠roads and conducting emergency treatment, the army said.

A Buddhist monk looks at photographs of missing and deceased people pasted on wall outside Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital, following flash floods and a mudslide, in Kathmandu, Nepal, Tuesday. At least 4,000 people remained missing as the death toll crossed 1,000. (Photo: Monika Malla, Reuters)

"We did not have the time to grab anything before fleeing," said a survivor from the hard-hit Rasuwa district, who said she had walked to Nuwakot with scores of other villagers who survived. "What we were wearing is the only pair of clothes we have. And even they are wet from rain."

Rescue teams had managed to restore road networks to Nuwakot, one of the worst-affected districts, facilitating rescue operations and distribution of relief material, Shah said.

Foreign help flows in

In China, rescue teams worked through the night to reopen access to the Nepali border, on a steep mountain gorge with unstable cliffs on one side and ‌fast-flowing river channels on the other.

Beijing will send DNA testing experts to disaster-hit areas as well as a second batch of ​relief supplies, its foreign ministry said, adding that equipment would include drones and water purification.

South Korea, nine of whose nationals were working at a hydropower project and are missing, also said it will send a 44-member emergency relief team to support search and rescue operations in the Rasuwa region.

Nepal last week turned down foreign involvement in general search and rescue but said it needed specialized services and advanced technological support in areas such as life-detecting machines, large refrigerators and prefabricated bridges.

Aid worth more than $42 million had poured into the country after the disaster, Shah said, and the government expected the contributions to increase.

Rescue efforts focus on hydropower stations

Shah said 279 workers had been rescued from hydropower projects, with joint teams from Nepal, India and China working on search-and-rescue operations.

Rescue teams drained water from tunnel heads and used rock breakers to make entry ​paths into the tunnels, Nepal's army said, as troops tried to reach those still believed to be trapped inside.

"Our first rescue observation at Trishuli Hydro Power plant shows that it is not humanly possible to go into the ‌tunnel," Asish Gurung, ‌a mountain guide helping in the tunnel ⁠rescue, told Reuters from Haku village in Rasuwa district.

"We need machines like bulldozers and excavators. There are two of them here now. One is not functioning and the other is being repaired. There may be about 500 people trapped inside," he said.

Rescue personnel work at a hydropower tunnel site in the aftermath of deadly flash floods and a mudslide, in Rasuwa district, Nepal, in this still image obtained from a social media video released on Monday. Aid worth over $42 million has already arrived in the country, Prime Minister Balendra Shah said on Tuesday. (Photo: Naveen Srivastava via X)

There has been a boom in hydropower projects in Nepal since the turn of the century as the mountainous country sought to take advantage of its Himalayan water resources to address chronic domestic power shortages and exploit prospects for selling electricity to southern neighbor India.

Shah said the disaster signaled the ‌growing risks the Himalayan region faces from a ​warming planet.

"The time has come for us to strongly raise before the international community the disasters we ‌are experiencing as a consequence of climate change," ⁠Shah said in his post.

Last week's flood ​was "caused by glacier instability under the long-term effects of global warming," China's state broadcaster said on Monday.

काठमाण्डू, नेपाल : नेपाल केरऽ बाढ़ म॑ मृतकऽ के संख्या १,००० पार करी गेलै, कैन्हेंकि बचावकर्मी न॑ भारी मशीनरी, हेलीकॉप्टर आरू एक्सकेवेटर के इस्तेमाल करी क॑ हजारों लोगऽ के पास पहुँचैलकै, जेकरऽ लगभग एक सप्ताह बाद ही विनाशकारी हिमालयी आपदा शहर आरू घाटी भर म॑ विनाश के निशान छोड़ी गेलऽ छै ।

चीन, भारत आरू नेपाल केरऽ विशेष बचाव दल न॑ दूरस्थ इलाका तलक पहुँचै लेली अस्थायी पुल बनैलकै आरू हिमालय म॑ जलविद्युत परियोजना के खंडहर के माध्यम स॑ खोदलकै, जेकरा म॑ खुदाई के इस्तेमाल करी क॑ सुरंगऽ के भीतर फंसलऽ करीब ३०० मजदूरऽ क॑ बचाबै के काम करलऽ गेलै ।

26 अगस्त क॑ ग्लेशियर केरऽ गिरला स॑ चीन के साथ गरीब राष्ट्र केरऽ सीमावर्ती क्षेत्र म॑ बर्फ, चट्टान आरू कीचड़ के बाढ़ आबी गेलऽ छेलै ।

देश केरऽ आपदा प्रबंधन प्राधिकरण न॑ मंगलवार क॑ कहलकै कि कम स॑ कम ६३९ लोग कईएक तबाह जलविद्युत स्टेशनऽ म॑ फंसलऽ छै जे बचाव प्रयासऽ के ⁠केन्द्र बनी गेलऽ छै ।

कुल पुष्टि मृत्यु के संख्या बढ़ी क॑ १,००३ होय गेलै, जेकरा म॑ लगभग ४,००० लोग अखनी तलक लापता छै, जेकरा म॑ ३९ देशऽ के ५९० विदेशी ⁠राष्ट्रीय लोग भी शामिल छै ।

प्रधानमंत्री बलेन्द्र शाह सोमदिन देर राति सोशल मीडिया पोस्ट मे कहलनि जे, हजारों नागरिक के घर, परिवार, प्रियजन आ संपत्ति के नुकसान भेल अछि।

ओ कहलनि जे, पूरा प्रभावित क्षेत्र मे 11 हजार सं बेसी लोक के बचाओल गेल अछि, आओर किछु इलाका मे बिजली आ संचार लाइन के बहाल कायल गेल अछि, जाहि सं विस्थापित लोक के समर्थन के वादा कएल गेल अछि.

सेना न॑ कहलकै कि ⁠प्रभावित क्षेत्रऽ म॑ ९,२०० स॑ भी अधिक जवान क॑ तैनात करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै, जेकरा म॑ घायलऽ के खोज आरू बचाव के समन्वय करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै, शव के प्रबंधन म॑ सहायता करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै, अवरुद्ध ⁠सड़क खोललऽ गेलऽ छेलै आरू आपातकालीन इलाज करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै ।

नेपाल के काठमांडू मे मंगलदिन त्रिभुवन विश्वविद्यालय शिक्षण अस्पताल के बाहर, झटका बाढ़ आ कीचड़ के बाद देबाल पर चिपकल लापता आ मृत लोक के फोटो देखैत बौद्ध भिक्षु। मृतकक संख्या एक हजार पार भेला स कम स कम चारि हजार लोक लापता रहल। (फोटो: मोनिका मल्ला, रायटर)

कड़ा प्रभावित रसुवा जिला के एकटा बचि गेल महिला कहलनि जे, हमरा सब लग भागबा सं पहिने किछु हड़पबाक समय नहि छल, जे कहलनि जे ओ बचल दर्जनों अन्य ग्रामीण के संग पैदल नुवाकोट पहुंचल छलीह। "हमरा सभ जे पहिरने रही से एकमात्र जोड़ी कपड़ा अछि। आओर ओहो बरखासँ भीजल अछि।"

शाह कहलनि जे, बचाव दल सबस बेसी प्रभावित जिला मे सं एक नुवाकोट के सड़क नेटवर्क के बहाल करय मे सफल रहल छल, जाहि सं बचाव कार्य आ राहत सामग्री के वितरण मे सुविधा भेल छल।

विदेशी मदद बहैत अछि

चीन में बचाव दल रात भर नेपाली सीमा तक पहुंच के फेर सं खोलय के काज केलक, जे एक कात अस्थिर चट्टान आ दोसर कात तेजी सं बहय वाला नदी के चैनल वाला खड़ा पहाड़ी गॉर्ज पर छल.

ओकरऽ विदेश मंत्रालय न॑ कहलकै कि बीजिंग आपदा प्रभावित क्षेत्रऽ म॑ डीएनए जांच विशेषज्ञऽ के साथ-साथ राहत आपूर्ति केरऽ दोसरऽ बैच भी भेजतै आरू कहलकै कि उपकरणऽ म॑ ड्रोन आरू पानी शुद्धिकरण शामिल होतै ।

दक्षिण कोरिया, जेकरऽ नौ नागरिक जलविद्युत परियोजना म॑ काम करी रहलऽ छेलै आरू लापता छै, न॑ ई भी कहलकै कि वू रसुवा क्षेत्र म॑ खोज आरू बचाव अभियान म॑ सहायता लेली ४४ सदस्यीय आपातकालीन राहत टीम भेजतै ।

नेपाल पिछला सप्ताह सामान्य खोज आ बचाव मे विदेशी संलग्नता ठुकरा देलक मुदा जीवन पता लगाबय वाला मशीन, पैघ फ्रिज आ पूर्वनिर्मित पुल जेहन क्षेत्र मे विशेष सेवा आ उन्नत तकनीकी सहयोग के जरूरत अछि।

शाह कहलनि जे, आपदा के बाद देश मे 4.2 करोड़ डॉलर सं बेसी के सहायता के बरसात भ गेल छल आ सरकार के उम्मीद अछि जे एहि मे योगदान बढ़त.

full_article:
(TNND) — The death toll from catastrophic flash flooding along the Nepal-China border has surpassed 1,000 as rescue teams search through mud, rocks and debris for thousands of people still missing.

About 80 Americans remained unaccounted for on Monday, according to the latest public State Department update per Fox News, while 13 U.S. citizens had made their way to safety.

Nepal’s disaster agency said 1,003 people had been confirmed dead and 3,916 remained missing, including 583 foreign nationals. China, in its latest update, reported 16 deaths and 546 people missing, including 261 foreigners.

Nepalese authorities have begun burying unidentified bodies in temporary graves as they preserve DNA samples, photograph distinguishing features and record other details to help families identify and claim the remains later.

Rescuers are also racing to reach workers believed trapped in damaged hydropower tunnels. About 900 workers are missing from 12 projects, and local authorities believe roughly 500 may be trapped underground.

Nepalese authorities said at least 11,814 people have been rescued so far. Helicopters and other aircraft have been used to reach stranded communities after flooding and landslides destroyed roads and bridges.

China is sending a second batch of relief supplies to Nepal, including drones, DNA-testing equipment and water-purification supplies, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said. Chinese DNA experts will also help identify bodies.

The disaster began when a glacial collapse in the Himalayas sent rock, ice and meltwater into valleys below, unleashing powerful flooding downstream. Scientists analyzing satellite imagery said the collapse appears to have involved bedrock failing beneath a glacier and was powerful enough to register as a magnitude 5.2 seismic event.

TRISHULI, NEPAL - AUGUST 30: A view of damaged tunnel of the Trishuli Hydropower Plant on the banks of the swollen Trishuli River following landslides on August 30, 2026, in Trishuli, Nepal. (Photo by Ritesh Shukla/Getty Images)

The surge swept through river valleys in Tibet and Nepal, destroying homes, roads and bridges and carrying mud and debris downstream.

Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah said the disaster underscored the growing climate risks facing the Himalayan region.

“This incident has indicated that the risks we face in the Himalayan region are increasing with climate change,” Shah wrote Monday night. “Therefore, this region must be alert, and at the same time, it is time for us to strongly raise the issue of disasters caused by climate change before the international community.”

title: China-Nepal flood is a warning from a warming planet - People's World
description: China-Nepal flood is a warning from a warming planet  People's World
publisher.title: People's World
full_article:
Disaster response personnel carry the body of a flash flood victim for burial at a mass grave in Chitwan, Nepal, Aug. 31, 2026. | Dar Yasin / AP

The speed at which a glacier can become a disaster was revealed high in the Himalayas last week, at an elevation of roughly 5,200 meters (17,000 feet), when a glacier near the China-Nepal border fractured, unleashing a cascade of rock and ice. But what began as an ice avalanche soon became a high-speed debris flow and then turned into a catastrophic mudslide.

By the time it reached Gyirong Port in China’s Xizang autonomous region, it was hurtling at roughly 180 kilometers (112 miles) per hour. The entire sequence from the initial collapse to the devastating arrival of the mudslide at Gyirong Port took only about seven minutes, leaving no time for prewarning and causing heavy casualties on both sides of the border.

Scientists have long warned that glaciers around the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and the broader Himalayan region—the so-called “Third Pole” and the largest body of ice outside the Arctic and Antarctic—are becoming increasingly unstable as the planet warms.

Glaciers are extraordinarily sensitive to temperature changes, and human-induced warming has been the primary driver of widespread glacial retreat since the 1990s. This continued melting does not merely make glaciers smaller but also destabilizes them, markedly increasing the likelihood of ice, rock, and water moving together. As the climate warms, such glacial chain disasters are becoming more frequent, more widespread, and more destructive.

The glacier was, in this case, more a messenger than a culprit. The years from 2015 through 2025 were the 11 hottest on record. Global greenhouse-gas emissions reached a record high, while glaciers worldwide lost an estimated 408 billion metric tons of mass in 2025 alone—equivalent to filling five Olympic-sized swimming pools every second of the year. The Himalayas are among the regions that suffered the greatest losses.

Yet, when such disasters occur, responsibility is often discussed as though emissions were neatly confined within national borders. They are not.

A smartphone assembled in Asia does not become environmentally benign because its eventual buyer lives in California. National emissions inventories by country generally count pollution where production occurs, even if production serves consumption elsewhere. The result is a peculiar accounting system in which wealthy societies consume carbon-intensive goods while much of the associated pollution appears on somebody else’s ledger.

For instance, while the U.S.’ territorial energy-related carbon dioxide emissions reached roughly 4.9 billion metric tons in 2025, its consumption footprint is significantly higher, revealing the carbon cost of outsourcing production to other countries.

This matters because the climate crisis is fundamentally a question of cumulative emissions. The U.S. alone is responsible for roughly one-fifth of all cumulative carbon dioxide emissions since 1850, with the European Union accounting for about 12%. Taken together, developed nations have emitted 60 to 65% of all greenhouse gases while representing less than 15% of the world’s population.

Rescuers wade through deep mud while carrying out search and rescue operations at the mudslide-hit Gyirong Port in Gyirong County, southwestern China’s Tibet Autonomous Region, on Aug. 29, 2026. | Lhasa Fire and Rescue Mobile Detachment / Xinhua News Agency

The developed economies have benefited enormously from over two centuries of carbon-intensive industrialization. They therefore cannot plausibly present themselves as innocent bystanders when the consequences of their prosperity manifest in poorer and more vulnerable parts of the world.

Nor is climate finance charity. The principle of common but differentiated responsibilities recognizes a basic fact: Countries share a common interest in stabilizing the climate, but they do not share identical histories or capacities.

The Paris Agreement explicitly requires developed countries to provide funds and technological support to developing nations. The pledge made in 2009 to mobilize $100 billion annually by 2020 was met two years late. Even now, the new target of $300 billion per year by 2035 remains a fraction of the $2.4 trillion that United Nations experts estimate developing countries actually need every year.

This makes the upcoming COP31 meeting in Antalya, Turkiye, more than just another diplomatic gathering. It should be a test of whether climate promises can evolve into practical solidarity. The conference is expected to address climate finance, the transition away from fossil fuels, and measures for building climate-resilient societies.

Will wealthy countries provide developing countries the finance and technology needed not merely to reduce emissions but also to survive the consequences of warming that are already unfolding? The old answer—that everyone is responsible, therefore everyone is equally responsible—is morally convenient but scientifically inadequate. A glacier does not know where a factory is registered. Carbon dioxide does not carry a passport.

The mudslide along the China-Nepal border should therefore be seen as a warning from our warming planet. The question at COP31 is whether the world’s wealthiest economies will heed this warning and acknowledge that helping vulnerable countries confront the consequences is not generosity but part of the bill for a crisis from which they have benefited for generations.

हिमालय म॑ जे गति स॑ आपदा बनी सकै छै, ओकरऽ खुलासा पिछला सप्ताह हिमालय म॑ लगभग ५,२०० मीटर (१७,००० फीट) के ऊंचाई प॑ करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै, जब॑ चीन-नेपाल सीमा के पास एगो ग्लेशियर टूटी गेलै, जेकरा स॑ चट्टान आरू बर्फ के झरना निकली गेलै । लेकिन जे बर्फ के हिमस्खलन के रूप में शुरू होलै, वू जल्दी ही तेज गति के मलबा के बहाव बनी गेलै आरू फेरू विनाशकारी कीचड़ में बदली गेलै ।

चीन केरऽ ज़िज़ांग स्वायत्त क्षेत्र केरऽ ग्यिरॉंग बंदरगाह पहुँचै तलक ई लगभग १८० किलोमीटर (११२ मील) प्रति घंटा के रफ्तार स॑ दौड़ी रहलऽ छेलै । शुरुआती पतन स॑ ल॑ क॑ ग्यिरॉंग बंदरगाह प॑ कीचड़ केरऽ विनाशकारी आगमन तक के पूरा क्रम म॑ मात्र लगभग सात मिनट लगलै, जेकरा स॑ पूर्व चेतावनी लेली समय नै बचलै आरू सीमा केरऽ दोनों तरफ भारी जानमाल के नुकसान पहुँचलै ।

वैज्ञानिक सब बहुत दिन स॑ चेतावनी द॑ रहलऽ छै कि किंघाई-तिब्बत पठार आरू व्यापक हिमालयी क्षेत्र के आसपास के ग्लेशियर - तथाकथित “तीसरा ध्रुव” आरू आर्कटिक आरू अंटार्कटिक के बाहर बर्फ केरऽ सबस॑ बड़ऽ निकाय- ग्रह के गर्मी के साथ-साथ तेजी स॑ अस्थिर होय रहलऽ छै ।

ग्लेशियर तापमान परिवर्तन के प्रति असाधारण रूप स॑ संवेदनशील छै, आरू मानव-प्रेरित गर्मी १९९० के दशक स॑ ही व्यापक हिमनदी पीछे हटै के प्राथमिक चालक रहलऽ छै । ई लगातार पिघलला स॑ ग्लेशियर खाली छोटऽ नै होय जाय छै बल्कि ओकरा अस्थिर भी होय जाय छै, जेकरा स॑ बर्फ, चट्टान आरू पानी के एक साथ चलै के संभावना काफी बढ़ी जाय छै । जेना-जेना जलवायु गर्म होय रहलऽ छै, ऐन्हऽ हिमनदी श्रृंखला केरऽ आपदा अधिक बार, अधिक व्यापक आरू अधिक विनाशकारी होय रहलऽ छै ।

ग्लेशियर, एहि मामला में, अपराधी सं बेसी दूत छल. 2015 स॑ 2025 तलक के साल रिकॉर्ड म॑ सबस॑ गरम 11 साल छेलै । वैश्विक ग्रीनहाउस-गैस उत्सर्जन रिकॉर्ड उच्चतम स्तर प॑ पहुँची गेलै, जबकि दुनिया भर म॑ ग्लेशियरऽ के द्रव्यमान म॑ लगभग ४०८ अरब मीट्रिक टन द्रव्यमान के नुकसान केवल २०२५ म॑ ही होय गेलै- जे साल केरऽ हर सेकंड म॑ ओलंपिक आकार के पांच स्विमिंग पूल भरला के बराबर छै । हिमालय ओहि क्षेत्र मे शामिल अछि जाहि मे सबस बेसी नुकसान भेल।

तइयो जखन एहन आपदा अबैत अछि त जिम्मेदारी पर अक्सरहां एहन चर्चा होइत अछि जेना उत्सर्जन राष्ट्रीय सीमाक भीतर सलीका सं सीमित भ गेल हो. ओ सभ नहि छथि।

एशिया म॑ इकट्ठा करलऽ गेलऽ स्मार्टफोन पर्यावरण के दृष्टि स॑ सौम्य नै होय छै, कैन्हेंकि एकरऽ अंतिम खरीदार कैलिफोर्निया म॑ रहै छै । देशक कें अनुसार राष्ट्रीय उत्सर्जन इन्वेंट्री आमतौर पर प्रदूषण कें गिनती करयत छै जत उत्पादन होयत छै, भले ही उत्पादन अन्यत्र खपत कें सेवा करयत छै. एकरऽ परिणाम एगो विचित्र लेखा प्रणाली छै जेकरा म॑ धनी समाज कार्बन-गहन वस्तु के खपत करै छै जबकि एकरा स॑ जुड़लऽ बहुत सारा प्रदूषण ककरो दोसरऽ के लेजर प॑ दिखाई दै छै ।

उदाहरण लेली, जबकि अमेरिका केरऽ क्षेत्रीय ऊर्जा स॑ संबंधित कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड उत्सर्जन २०२५ म॑ लगभग ४.९ अरब मीट्रिक टन तलक पहुँची गेलऽ छै, लेकिन एकरऽ खपत केरऽ पदचिह्न काफी अधिक छै, जेकरा स॑ उत्पादन क॑ अन्य देशऽ क॑ आउटसोर्सिंग करै के कार्बन लागत के खुलासा करलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

ई महत्वपूर्ण छै, कैन्हेंकि जलवायु संकट मौलिक रूप स॑ संचयी उत्सर्जन के सवाल छै । 1850 स॑ अब तलक के सब संचयी कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड उत्सर्जन केरऽ लगभग पांचवा हिस्सा लेली असगरे अमेरिका जिम्मेदार छै, जेकरा म॑ यूरोपीय संघ केरऽ हिस्सा लगभग 12% छै । एकरा मिला क॑ देखलऽ जाय त॑ विकसित राष्ट्रऽ न॑ सब ग्रीनहाउस गैसऽ के ६० स॑ ६५% उत्सर्जन करलकै जबकि दुनिया केरऽ १५% स॑ भी कम आबादी के प्रतिनिधित्व करलकै ।

चीन केरऽ दक्षिण-पश्चिमी तिब्बत स्वायत्त क्षेत्र केरऽ ग्यिरॉंग काउंटी म॑ कीचड़ स॑ प्रभावित ग्यिरॉंग बंदरगाह प॑ 29 अगस्त, 2026 क॑ खोज आरू बचाव अभियान चलाबै के दौरान बचावकर्मी गहरी कीचड़ स॑ गुजरी रहलऽ छै ।| ल्हासा फायर एंड रेस्क्यू मोबाइल टुकड़ी / सिन्हुआ न्यूज एजेंसी

दू शताब्दी स॑ भी अधिक समय स॑ कार्बन-प्रधान औद्योगीकरण स॑ विकसित अर्थव्यवस्था क॑ बहुत फायदा मिललऽ छै । अतः ई सब व्यावहारिक रूप स अपना कए निर्दोष दर्शक क रूप मे नहि प्रस्तुत क सकैत छथि जखन हुनकर समृद्धि क परिणाम दुनिया क गरीब आ बेसी कमजोर हिस्सा मे प्रकट होइत अछि ।

आ ने जलवायु वित्त चैरिटी अछि। साझा लेकिन विभेदित जिम्मेदारी के सिद्धांत एकटा मूलभूत तथ्य के पहचान करै छै: देशऽ के जलवायु क॑ स्थिर करै म॑ साझा हित छै, लेकिन ओकरऽ इतिहास या क्षमता एक जैसनऽ नै छै ।

पेरिस समझौता म॑ स्पष्ट रूप स॑ विकसित देशऽ स॑ विकासशील राष्ट्रऽ क॑ धन आरू तकनीकी सहायता प्रदान करै के कहलऽ गेलऽ छै । 2020 तक सालाना 100 अरब डॉलर जुटाबै के प्रतिज्ञा 2009 मे दू साल देरी स पूरा भेल। अखनी भी 2035 तलक प्रति वर्ष 300 अरब डॉलर केरऽ नया लक्ष्य वू 2.4 खरब डॉलर केरऽ एगो हिस्सा बनलऽ छै जेकरऽ अनुमान संयुक्त राष्ट्र केरऽ विशेषज्ञऽ के अनुमान छै कि विकासशील देशऽ क॑ वास्तव म॑ हर साल जरूरत छै ।

ई स॑ तुर्की केरऽ अंटाल्या म॑ होबै वाला सीओपी३१ केरऽ बैठक खाली एगो आरू कूटनीतिक सभा स॑ अधिक होय गेलऽ छै । ई एकरऽ परीक्षा होना चाहियऽ कि जलवायु वादा व्यावहारिक एकजुटता म॑ विकसित होय सकै छै कि नै । उम्मीद छै कि ई सम्मेलन म॑ जलवायु वित्त, जीवाश्म ईंधन स॑ दूर संक्रमण, आरू जलवायु-लचीली समाज के निर्माण के उपायऽ प॑ ध्यान देलऽ जैतै ।

की धनी देश विकासशील देशक कें ओ वित्त आ तकनीक उपलब्ध करायत जेकर जरूरत छै केवल उत्सर्जन कें कम करय कें लेल नहि बल्कि गर्मी कें परिणाम सं बचय कें लेल जे पहिने सं खुल रहल छै? पुरान उत्तर-जे सब जिम्मेदार अछि, तेँ सब कियो समान रूप सँ जिम्मेदार अछि-नैतिक रूप सँ सुविधाजनक अछि मुदा वैज्ञानिक रूप सँ अपर्याप्त अछि । ग्लेशियर के पता नै छै कि फैक्ट्री कतय पंजीकृत छै। कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड मे पासपोर्ट नहि होइत अछि।

एहि लेल चीन-नेपाल सीमा पर भेल थाल-कादो केँ हमरा लोकनिक वार्मिंग ग्रह सँ चेतावनी बुझबाक चाही। सीओपी31 म॑ सवाल ई छै कि की दुनिया केरऽ सबसें धनी अर्थव्यवस्था ई चेतावनी प॑ ध्यान देतै आरू ई बात क॑ स्वीकार करतै कि कमजोर देशऽ क॑ एकरऽ परिणाम के सामना करै म॑ मदद करना उदारता नै बल्कि एगो ऐसनऽ संकट केरऽ बिल के हिस्सा छै, जेकरा स॑ ओकरा पीढ़ी-दर-पीढ़ी फायदा होय रहलऽ छै ।

आशा अछि जे अहाँ सब एहि लेख के सराहना केलौं। पीपुल्स वर्ल्ड मे हमर मानब अछि जे खबर आ जानकारी मुफ्त आ सबहक लेल सुलभ होबाक चाही, मुदा हमरा सभ के अहां सभ के मदद के जरूरत अछि. हमरऽ पत्रकारिता कॉरपोरेट प्रभाव आरू पेवाल स॑ मुक्त छै, कैन्हेंकि हम्में पूर्ण रूप स॑ पाठक समर्थित छियै । केवल अहाँ हमर पाठक आ समर्थक लोकनि ई संभव करैत छी । अगर अहां सभ के पीपुल्स वर्ल्ड आओर हम सभ जे कहानी अनैत छी ओकरा पढ़य मे नीक लगैत अछि त आईये दान द क या मासिक सस्टेनर बनि हमर काज के सहयोग करिऔ. अहां कें धन्यवाद!

full_article:
A final accounting of lives lost is expected to be in thousands. In the Chitwan district of southern Nepal, some 120 miles from the mountain valleys where the glacial fury first struck, officials have buried nearly 200 unidentified bodies in a forested area because of a lack of morgue space. Mass burials have also started in a forest outside Kathmandu, the capital. DNA samples have been collected so the bodies can be identified later.

Families are still waiting outside hospitals in Kathmandu, the capital, for news of their loved ones. “Even if it’s just their bodies, at least we’d know,” Dil Kumari Masrangi Magar, a woman from Udaypur district in southeastern Nepal, told me outside Kathmandu’s Teaching Hospital. Magar was searching for her missing brother-in-law and a nephew, and had pasted their photos on a hospital wall already covered with images of the dead and names of the missing.

full_article:
On August 26, a glacier collapsed on the Nepal-China border, sending a catastrophic debris flow more than 60 miles downstream along the Trishuli River, wiping out bridges, roads, and settlements across a vast stretch of northern Nepal. Communities were cut off entirely—reachable only by helicopter or on foot. WCK mobilized immediately and teams are now cooking from a community kitchen in the hardest hit area.

Our early focus was Nuwakot Province, where evacuees were being airlifted to a makeshift airfield in Bidur. Families waited at the gates, straining for a familiar face. The moment survivors landed, WCK and our partners were waiting with a hot meal.

Through the first few days of the response, WCK has served thousands of meals—including local staples like samosas and momos.

Today, our teams began operations at our first community kitchen in Gerkhutar, just north of Bidur. Working alongside the Chefs Association of Nepal, we are serving breakfast, lunch, and dinner to families there. Our team overcame significant obstacles to open this kitchen. Road conditions meant traveling just seven miles took over five hours. Thanks to the local knowledge of Nepal Scouts, a national scouting and guiding organization, all the equipment arrived safely.

Two more community kitchens open tomorrow. Community kitchens remain our preferred approach wherever conditions allow. Culturally, people here strongly prefer cooking their own food.

WCK Meal Recipient Locations

As road conditions north of Bidur improve, we are mobilizing more equipment to ensure kitchen teams have everything they need to cook at scale.

The danger to community members is not over. A new barrier lake near the Nepal-China border poses ongoing flood risk, and forecasters are warning of severe flash flooding from local waterways. WCK teams are monitoring conditions closely and will keep serving for as long as communities need us.

A British male has been rescued in Nepal almost a week after devastating floods, which have killed more than 1,000 people.

The British national, who has not been named, was saved alongside 118 Nepalese people on Tuesday.

Speaking at a press conference in Nepal, an army spokesperson said: “Regarding today’s rescue, since 1700 hours we have rescued 118 Nepalese people.

“Out of the 118, 44 were female and 74 were male, and we have also rescued one British male during this search and rescue operation, and the search and rescue operation is continuing.

The death toll rose to 1,050, while about 4,000 people remain missing, ​including ⁠583 foreign nationals.

The disaster left at least 2.2 million tonnes of debris, according to a preliminary estimate by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), including parts of buildings, rocks, and sediment.

“The amount of debris shows the scale of the destruction and the challenge communities face as ⁠they clear homes, roads and public spaces and begin to rebuild,” it said.

More than 11,000 people have been rescued, and power and communication lines ​were restored ⁠in some areas, prime minister Balendra Shah said in a ‌social media post on Monday.

Shah said 279 workers were rescued from hydropower projects, with joint teams from Nepal, India and China working on search-and-rescue operations.

On Saturday, a rapid deployment team from the UK arrived in Nepal to provide support for Britons and their families.

The team, comprising specially trained crisis response staff, will work alongside the British embassy and local authorities to support British nationals arriving at and departing from the airport, as well as those seeking information about missing relatives.

The team will liaise with local authorities and emergency responders, reinforce existing consular operations on the ground, and work with families in the UK concerned for loved ones.

It forms part of the UK’s wider response to the flooding, which includes £5m of humanitarian support for relief and recovery efforts.

full_article:
RICHMOND, Va. (WWBT) - A Virginia-based nonprofit is on the ground in Nepal delivering food to families impacted by the catastrophic flood.

Mercy Chefs often provides hot meals to those in need, but pivoted to grocery packs for Nepal’s unique situation.

Many places are only accessible by helicopter.

“Most of the bridges have been wiped out. So, to get to the communities on the far side, you have to go hours around to find a bridge that’s operable to get to that community, and these people didn’t have margin beforehand. What little they had is now either gone or it’s under 20 or 30 feet of mud at this point,” Mercy Chefs Chief Global Officer Carl Ladd said.

Ladd was on the ground in Nuwakot on Tuesday, September 1, and has been in the country for several days now. In that time, he and his team have helped provide around 75,000 meals.

The packs contain 30 days of food rations, so people will be set for the coming days.

“Most of the families we’re distributing to have lost loved ones; they’ve lost their home, they’ve lost their livelihood, they’ve lost their farm. So it’s devastating,” Ladd said.

Mercy Chefs is working with local Nepali organizations throughout the effort, which Ladd says has been key.

Ladd has been on the ground for other natural disasters, and says typically in floods there’s a couple feet of sediment, but this time the debris extends all throughout the river valley.

“In most of these places there’s still 20 feet of sediment and so two-story buildings are underneath mud for whole towns,” Ladd said.

Ladd describes the entire experience as humbling, from seeing a sigh of relief on a mother’s face, to working with local volunteers.

Virginians are among some of the people still unaccounted for, which puts things in perspective for the Mercy Chefs team. Its crew is keeping them and their loved ones in mind during the mission.

“I would say that’s a really unique thing about this disaster is the amount of foreigners that were affected. Obviously, it’s a really popular destination and valley for trekking,” Ladd said. “It makes the world a little bit smaller and it hit a little bit more closer to home. And realizing that the international community is affected and obviously the Nepalese communities is largely affected.”

Mercy Chefs will continue to be in Nepal as long as its team is needed. Donations to the effort can be made here.

full_article:
CHARLESTON, S.C. (WRDW/WAGT) - Water Mission disaster response teams, including people from the Charleston area, arrived in the Nepal-China border region Tuesday, with some already traveling to deliver aid, following mudslides and flash floods that struck nearly a week ago.

Mount Pleasant resident Kristin Parker said she is concerned for loved ones in the area.

Her family lived in Nepal for 13 years, and she has visited the border region where the flooding originated, keeping close ties with villagers there.

“It’s horrible for me to think about when I watch it from a different distance, but to really know people that are living it,” Kristin Parker, cofounder of Shared City and Mount Pleasant resident, said.

As of today, CBS reports at least 1,050 dead and over 4,600 missing in Nepal.

Across the border in Tibet, Chinese officials confirm 16 deaths and more than 550 people still missing.

Officials in Nepal say a massive rock and ice avalanche in the mountains likely triggered the flooding.

According to CBS News, 85 Americans are still listed as missing.

“We’re still finding out the extent of the loss, but even already we know that there are some families where there’s only one family member left,” Parker said.

Search teams have rescued more than 11,000 survivors, but many remain cut off from basic necessities.

Charleston-based Water Mission is deploying teams with specialized testing gear to secure safe water.

“Water supply is often contaminated or non-existent and in order to rebuild and restart, having access to safe drinking water is so important,” said Gregg Dinino, public relations director for Water Mission.

On-the-ground engineers are testing local sources, installing treatment systems and teaching local volunteers how to keep them running.

“It’s difficult; they’re very hard to reach areas, you have to traverse a mountain into the Himalayas. Many of these roads have been knocked out. We’ve heard from contacts on the ground that what used to take 45 minutes to get to an area now takes six to seven hours,” Dinino said.

The organization sets up tap stands to serve as central distribution points for residents.

By treating water directly at the source, the systems can generate thousands of gallons daily, enough to supply up to 5,000 survivors each day.

“So thankful for the work they do and I just feel so relieved that they’re going to be on the ground to care about the people that I love so much there,” Parker said.

Dinino said local volunteers in Charleston are critical for assembling and preparing equipment for disaster relief.

He said the duration of their deployment relies heavily on donations.

Those interested in volunteering or donating through Water Mission can find more information on the Water Mission website.

जमीन पर इंजीनियर स्थानीय स्रोत कें परीक्षण कयर रहल छै, उपचार प्रणाली लगा रहल छै आ स्थानीय स्वयंसेवक कें सिखा रहल छै कि ओकरा कोना चलाएल जै.

डिनिनो कहलकै, "ई मुश्किल छै; ई सब इलाका में पहुँचना बहुत मुश्किल छै, हिमालय में पहाड़ पार करी क' जाय छै। ई सब में से बहुत सड़क के खटखटाय देलऽ गेलऽ छै। हम्में जमीन पर संपर्क सें सुनले छियै कि जेकरा में पहलें कोनो इलाका में पहुँचै में 45 मिनट लगै छेलै, ओकरा अब॑ छह से सात घंटा लगै छै।"

संगठन निवासीक कें लेल केंद्रीय वितरण बिंदु कें रूप मे काज करय कें लेल नल स्टैंड कें स्थापना करय छै.

ROBBINSVILLE, N.J. (WPVI) -- As rescue efforts continue following the deadly flash flooding in Nepal, a New Jersey woman is among those reported missing, while relief organizations work to assist survivors.

BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham in Robbinsville, the largest Hindu temple in the United States, is among the organizations helping support relief efforts.

The temple, which volunteers say has welcomed more than 4 million visitors over the past three years, is known as a place where many come to find peace.

READ MORE | Death toll tops 1,000 after Nepal flooding, as search continues for thousands

Rescuers are desperately searching for survivors after the devastating flooding on the border of Nepal and Tibet.

"The fundamental idea is to be a good person," said volunteer Yogesh Patel.

That message has taken on added significance as members of the temple and the larger BAPS temple community respond to flash floods in Nepal that have killed more than 1,000 people.

Patel said the scale and speed of the disaster were difficult to comprehend.

"It just seemed like this is not possible how can a wall of water that big literally go down a hill into valley and flood areas in seconds?" Patel said.

The Robbinsville temple is one of several BAPS temples sending aid to Nepal through a group in India. Patel said BAPS volunteers in Nepal began relief efforts immediately after the disaster.

"We actually have a center in Nepal, so our volunteers with BAPS from day 1 were active in trying to get grains, rice, lentils, food, cooking utensils and getting it to the worst affected areas as soon as possible," Patel said.

In addition to providing supplies, the temple's spiritual leader has offered prayers for those who died and for the thousands of people who remain unaccounted for. Those reported missing include Mukti Belahal of Princeton Junction.

"For those loved ones to not know where their loved ones are, it really is crushing," Patel said.

As search-and-rescue operations continue, volunteers say efforts to deliver food, supplies and other necessities to affected communities remain ongoing.

"Our hearts immediately go out to those who are suffering in this," Patel said.

Temple leaders said they hope the spirit of service promoted at BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham encourages others to offer positive thoughts and prayers for those affected by the disaster in Nepal.

title: Live updates: Warning signs were visible ahead of Nepal-China floods, report says - CNN
description: Live updates: Warning signs were visible ahead of Nepal-China floods, report says  CNNDeath toll from devastating floods in Nepal and China surpasses 1,000  Al JazeeraScenes of devastation in Nuwakot district after Nepal flash floods kill hundreds of people  Yahoo
publisher.title: CNN
full_article:
The glacier that collapsed causing a devastating landslide and flooding had visible signs of change days ahead of the disaster, according to a new report from a consortium of scientists.

“In hindsight, there were some pre-event indications,” including melt water that had turned visibly brown and signs of a crack propagating into the surrounding bedrock slope days before the collapse, scientists said in a report published last week.

The report – which also suggests more comprehensive early warning systems downstream could have saved a “significant number of lives” – comes as the catastrophe has shown what experts say is a need for better warning systems in a vast Himalayan region that is difficult to monitor.

Chinese and Nepali authorities had met as recently as May to discuss bolstering cooperation on monitoring natural hazards in the Himalayas, a government official who was present at that meeting told CNN.

Early warning systems had been set up recently in this region, focusing on several glacial lakes in China, but no operational system was set up in this area for glacier-related hazards, according to the report from the HiRISK scientific consortium, which monitors risk data in mountain environments.

Once the collapse started, however, the warning times from conventional systems would have likely been insufficient for evacuation at a border checkpoint that was among the first areas hit – given just how fast the initial landslide was moving. Further downstream, with warning times of 10 minutes or more, comprehensive systems could have saved lives, the scientists said.

Other experts have said that the glacial collapse highlights the urgency of better monitoring programs – and cooperation between countries – to detect changes.

“There is almost no way that anyone could have detected this event prior – it happened in a blind spot … (making it) extremely difficult to detect,” Austin Lord, a senior fellow in the Energy, Water and Sustainability program at the Stimson Center, wrote in a recent commentary.

He also highlighted “how greater communication, information sharing, and collaborative analysis of transboundary risks between Nepal and China are sorely needed.”

full_article: The death toll from Nepal's devastating floods surpassed 1,000 on Tuesday as rescuers deployed heavy machinery, helicopters and excavators to reach thousands still missing nearly a week after the Himalayan disaster tore through towns and valleys. Specialized rescue teams from China, India and Nepal built temporary bridges to reach remote areas and dug through the ruins of hydropower projects, using excavators to try to rescue nearly 300 workers trapped inside tunnels.

full_article:
KATHMANDU, Nepal (AP) — Rescue teams with search dogs continued to search through mud, rocks and debris on Tuesday on the border with Nepal and China for thousands of people still missing following the catastrophic floods that tore through communities across the Himalayas , leaving more than 1,000 dead.

As police in Kathmandu buried dozens of bodies in multiple trenches, Nepal’s disaster agency said that 1,003 deaths had been counted there, with 3,916 people missing, including 583 foreign nationals. In its latest update, China reported 16 deaths and 546 missing, including 261 foreigners.

The scale of the Aug. 26 disaster is hampering rescue efforts in both countries, with landslides, destroyed roads and widespread damage cutting off remote areas. Crews faced challenging conditions as they searched unstable terrain and piles of debris, raising fears the death toll could rise as rescuers reach isolated communities.

At least 168 people were killed and more than 1,300 were missing after catastrophic and deadly torrents of floods and mud swept through several communities along the Nepal-China following a glacier collapse.

Rescuers are racing to reach hundreds of workers believed to be trapped inside tunnels at hydropower projects in Nepal damaged by the floods. About 900 workers are missing from 12 projects, with roughly 500 believed to be trapped in tunnels, according to local authorities.

Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet, Nepal’s army spokesperson, said teams assisted by foreign experts were working at several hydropower projects. Images released by the army showed rescue teams entering debris-filled tunnels and wading through mud and water in the search for signs of life.

Mass burials of unidentified bodies in Kathmandu

In Kathmandu, police worked in heavy rain on Tuesday to bury dozens of bodies in multiple trenches next to a forested area.

Barbed wire was erected around the site, while blue numbered markers identified the graves of people whose names were not yet known.

Authorities in Nepal have been burying bodies in temporary graves until they can be identified. They are preserving DNA samples, photographing distinguishing facial features and recording other identifying details.

Each body is assigned a reference number to help families identify and claim the remains later.

Relief operations expanded to stranded communities

At least 11,814 people have been rescued so far, according to Nepalese authorities. Emergency crews used helicopters and other aircraft to reach stranded communities in areas where roads and bridges have been destroyed by the flooding and landslides.

Efforts are being stepped up to provide assistance to survivors in areas where roads and other transportation routes had been damaged or cut off.

China’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson, Guo Jiakun, said a second batch of relief supplies was being sent to Nepal, including drones, DNA testing and water purification equipment. Chinese DNA testing experts will also help Nepal identify bodies, he said.

Bimal Sharma, a helicopter pilot who has been flying rescue and relief missions, said he was shocked to see the devastation in Timure, a border town close to Tibet that he has known for years.

“It felt like I was flying over an entirely different landscape,” said Sharma, adding that he has had little opportunity to speak with the people he rescued. “I can see the pain in their eyes. It’s heartbreaking,” he said.

Glacial collapse in the Himalayas

The disaster began in the Himalayas when a glacial collapse sent large amounts of rock, ice and meltwater into valleys below, triggering powerful floods downstream.

Scientists studying satellite imagery said the collapse appears to have involved the failure of bedrock beneath a glacier in the Himalayan region. The rockfall was powerful enough to register as a magnitude 5.2 seismic event.

The resulting surge of water and debris entered rivers that flow through valleys in Tibet and Nepal, causing them to rise rapidly. Floodwaters swept away homes, buildings, roads and bridges and carried mud and rocks downstream.

Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah said that the disaster highlighted the need for action to combat climate change.

जाहि इलाका मे सड़क आ अन्य परिवहन मार्ग क्षतिग्रस्त या कटौती भ गेल छल, ओहि इलाका मे बचि गेल लोक कए मदद देबाक प्रयास तेज भ रहल अछि।

चीन के विदेश मंत्रालय के प्रवक्ता गुओ जियाकुन कहलनि जे, नेपाल मे राहत के दोसर बैच भेजल जा रहल अछि जाहि मे ड्रोन, डीएनए टेस्टिंग आ जल शुद्धिकरण उपकरण शामिल अछि। चीनी डीएनए परीक्षण विशेषज्ञ नेपाल के शव के पहचान करय मे सेहो मदद करत ओ कहलनि।

बचाव आरू राहत मिशन उड़ान भरै वाला हेलीकॉप्टर पायलट बिमल शर्मा नँ कहलकै कि तिब्बत के नजदीक सीमावर्ती शहर तिमुरे मँ तबाही देखी क हुनका चौंक गेलै, जेकरा हुनी सालौ स॑ जानत॑ छै ।

उपग्रह केरऽ इमेजरी के अध्ययन करै वाला वैज्ञानिकऽ न॑ कहलकै कि ई पतन म॑ हिमालयी क्षेत्र केरऽ एगो ग्लेशियर के नीचें बेडरोक केरऽ विफलता शामिल नजर आबी रहलऽ छै । ई चट्टान केरऽ गिरना एतना शक्तिशाली छेलै कि ५.२ परिमाण के भूकंपीय घटना के रूप म॑ पंजीकृत होय गेलै ।

एकरऽ परिणामस्वरूप पानी आरू मलबा केरऽ उफान तिब्बत आरू नेपाल केरऽ घाटी स॑ बहय वाला नदी म॑ प्रवेश करी क॑ तेजी स॑ बढ़ी गेलै । बाढ़िक पानि घर, भवन, सड़क आ पुल कए बहरा गेल आ थाल-कादो आ चट्टान कए नीचा ल गेल।
